# v 1.32.0

Thanks to @calebdw for the reports that led to a series of solid improvements.

## Highlights

- Improved microphone handling when using the system default input device.
- Fixed ONNX-ASR VAD routing so short dictations avoid unnecessary VAD trimming.
- Added a configurable ONNX-ASR VAD duration threshold.

## Configuration

New setting:

```jsonc
{
  "onnx_asr_vad_min_duration": 30
}
```

This is the minimum recording duration, in seconds, before ONNX-ASR routes audio through Silero VAD. Set it lower to use VAD more often, or higher to keep more recordings on direct recognition.

## Audio Device Management

- hyprwhspr now re-checks the current PulseAudio/PipeWire default microphone right before opening a recording stream when no explicit audio device is configured.
- Changing the system default microphone no longer requires restarting hyprwhspr for the next recording to use the new input.
- Stream startup retries now refresh the default input once before retrying, helping recover from transient PulseAudio/PipeWire host errors after a device change.
- The keepalive stream now moves to the refreshed default microphone when the default input changes.
- Explicitly configured audio devices remain sticky. If `audio_device_id` or `audio_device_name` is configured, hyprwhspr does not silently convert the setup into "follow system default" mode after a fallback.
- Device validation now rejects output-only devices when resolving defaults.
- Sounddevice default input updates now preserve the output device instead of overwriting the whole default device tuple.

## Hotplug Handling

- Audio hotplug events are now queued and dispatched serially through a worker thread.
- This keeps callback ordering predictable during noisy USB plug/unplug sequences.
- Device monitor startup failure now cleans up observer and worker state more completely.
- Device monitor shutdown now stops the dispatch worker cleanly.

## ONNX-ASR / Parakeet

- ONNX-ASR now keeps the direct model and VAD-wrapped model separate.
- Short recordings use direct recognition by default, avoiding aggressive speech-boundary trimming on normal dictation.
- Long recordings still use Silero VAD when `onnx_asr_use_vad` is enabled.
- Added `onnx_asr_vad_min_duration`, defaulting to `30` seconds, to control when ONNX-ASR switches from direct recognition to VAD-assisted recognition.
- Invalid VAD duration values fall back to `30` seconds, and negative values clamp to `0`.
- Model unload now clears the cached ONNX-ASR VAD model as well as the direct model.

## What's changed

### New: continuous recording mode

A new `"continuous"` recording mode that listens indefinitely and auto-transcribes whenever a pause in speech is detected.

Transcriptions are injected in real time as you speak, without pressing any key.

Enable via config or `hyprwhspr setup`:

```jsonc
{
    "recording_mode": "continuous"
}
```

> **Experimental.** See the [configuration docs](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) for silence threshold and floor-finding options. 

### Fix: language auto-detection on pywhispercpp backend (#160)

When `"language"` was `null` (the documented default for auto-detect), the pywhispercpp backend was silently falling back to whisper.cpp's compiled-in default of `"en"`, causing non-English speech to be transcribed as garbled English. The backend now calls `auto_detect_language()` explicitly when no language is set.

Users who pinned a language code (e.g. `"language": "fr"`) were unaffected.

### Feat: beam search decoding on pywhispercpp and faster-whisper backends (#159)

Both local backends now default to beam search with `beam_size: 5`, matching `whisper-cli` behavior. Previously, pywhispercpp used greedy decoding with no way to change it. The difference is most noticeable on non-English audio and noisier input.

Two new config keys:

```jsonc
{
    "sampling_strategy": "beam_search",  // "beam_search" (default) or "greedy"
    "beam_size": 5
}
```

`faster-whisper`'s previously hardcoded `beam_size: 5` also now respects the `beam_size` config key.

> **Note:** Changing `sampling_strategy` requires a service restart on the pywhispercpp backend.

### Fix: audio ducking timing

Audio ducking now activates after the stream is confirmed open rather than before, preventing a race where the duck fired before audio capture was ready.

### Fix: audio stream startup reliability

Improved retry logic on stream open to handle transient PortAudio errors (`-9987 paTimedOut`, `-9999` PulseAudio "No such entity") that could occur during service startup before the audio server had fully settled.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fix crash on startup with non-Cohere backends** ([#154](https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/issues/154))

  `get_credential` was re-imported as a local variable inside `initialize()` and `_reinitialize_cohere_transcribe()` in
`whisper_manager.py`. Python's scoping rules marked it local for the entire method at compile time, causing an
`UnboundLocalError` whenever a non-Cohere backend (`rest-api`, `realtime-ws`, `pywhispercpp`) was configured. Redundant local
imports removed; the module-level import is used throughout.

- **Fix USB microphone failures after idle on ALSA systems** ([#153](https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/issues/153))

  USB microphones managed via raw ALSA can power down after ~30 seconds of silence. When hyprwhspr tried to open the device for
the next recording, PortAudio's `PaUnixThread_New` timed out (`paTimedOut` / error -9987). This release introduces a silent
keepalive stream that holds the ALSA device open between recordings, preventing the kernel from suspending it. The keepalive is
only started when a multiplexed audio server (PipeWire or PulseAudio) is detected — on raw ALSA it is skipped to avoid holding
an exclusive lock that would block other applications.

  Additional hardening: stream start now retries up to 3 times with a brief pause on timeout, handling cold-start races on
service startup before the audio node has fully warmed up.

### Configuration

- New setting `stream_start_retry_delay` (default: `1.5` seconds) controls how long to wait between stream start retries on
timeout. Increase this value if your USB microphone frequently fails on the first recording after idle.

## Features

### Model unload / reload

Free GPU VRAM without stopping the service — useful before running a local LLM or other GPU-intensive application.

```bash
hyprwhspr model unload   # Unload model from GPU memory (service stays alive)
hyprwhspr model reload   # Reload model back into memory
```

- Recording is blocked while the model is unloaded, with a desktop notification on attempt
- Tray shows `󰒲` icon in `unloaded` state when the signal file is present
- Only applies to local backends (`pywhispercpp`, `faster-whisper`, `onnx-asr`); no-op for `rest-api` / `realtime-ws`
- Tip: bind to keys in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf`:
```
  bindd = SUPER ALT, U, Unload Whisper model, exec, hyprwhspr model unload
  bindd = SUPER ALT, L, Reload Whisper model, exec, hyprwhspr model reload
 ```

### Direct-type injection (inject_mode)

Adds a new inject_mode config option for terminals that use the Kitty keyboard protocol (Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm), where synthetic Ctrl+V keystrokes from ydotool are misinterpreted.

```
{ "inject_mode": "wtype" }
```

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `null` (default) | Clipboard + paste keystroke — existing behavior |
| `"wtype"` | Direct typing via `wtype` — works in all Wayland windows including Kitty-protocol terminals |
| `"ydotool_type"` | Direct typing via `ydotool type` — also works in Kitty-protocol terminals |

Both modes bypass the clipboard entirely and respect `auto_submit`. 

Gracefully falls back to clipboard+paste if the configured tool is not installed.

## Fixes

**hyprwhspr systemd status now streams output correctly**

Previously, systemctl output was silently captured when the service was active, and wrapped in [ERROR] tags when inactive or failed. 

Output now streams directly to the terminal in all cases.

**Single-character word_overrides now match mid-word and are case-insensitive**

Single-character overrides (e.g. "ß": "ss") previously used str.replace(), which missed uppercase variants and required exact case. They now use re.sub(..., re.IGNORECASE) without word boundaries, matching anywhere in a word — consistent with multi-character
override behavior.

```jsonc
{
    "word_overrides": { "ß": "ss" }
}
```

"Straße" → "Strasse", "Fuß" → "Fuss"

**Service starts without keyboard access when grab_keys: false (closes #139)**

When no keyboard devices are accessible and `grab_keys` is disabled, the service now starts successfully instead of exiting.

The shortcut is silently disabled; recording control falls back to the CLI (hyprwhspr record toggle) or the recording_control FIFO. 

Error messages also now suggest compositor bindings as an alternative when `grab_keys: false`.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/compare/v1.20.0...v1.21.0

## Bug fixes and improvements

* **Rapid-toggle race conditions** (https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/pull/134, @poberherr) — Several race conditions causing
broken behavior when pressing the recording shortcut in quick succession: the audio level monitoring thread was not being
replaced on rapid stop→start (leaving the mic OSD without level data), is_recording was being set outside the recording lock
allowing fast re-triggers to interleave incorrectly, and PipeWire default source changes were not being picked up on
re-initialization. The saved source from the mic picker is now restored on startup.

* **mic-osd crash on early SIGUSR1** (https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/pull/131, @poberherr) — The mic-osd daemon was being
killed before its signal handlers were registered, because Python's heavy imports (GTK4, numpy, etc.) took ~280ms while the
runner sent SIGUSR1 ~160ms after spawn — killing the process before the overlay could ever appear. Fixed by setting
SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 to SIG_IGN before imports, then installing real handlers once initialization completes.

* **Stale state files on crash or reboot** (https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/pull/128, @Nomadcxx) — If the service was killed
hard (SIGKILL, crash, reboot), state files like recording_status were left with stale values, causing hyprwhspr record toggle to
 always send stop instead of start. A new _reset_stale_state() now runs on both startup and graceful shutdown.

* `_keycode_to_name` crash (https://github.com/goodroot/hyprwhspr/pull/137, @mikecirioli) — Fixed a crash in the keyboard event loop
 when evdev returns a list of key names for a keycode instead of a single string.

## Features

Cancel recording - New ability to abort an in-progress recording and discard the audio without transcribing or injecting text. 

Useful when you hit your shortcut by accident or start speaking and want to bail out.

Three ways to cancel:

  - FIFO command: echo cancel > ~/.config/hyprwhspr/recording_control - bindable to any external hotkey manager
  - CLI: hyprwhspr record cancel
  - Dedicated shortcut: Set "cancel_shortcut": "SUPER+ESCAPE" (or any key combo) in config to get a native cancel key

Works in all recording modes including long-form, where it discards all accumulated segments and resets the session to idle.

# Release Notes

Stability is key! Please create issues as we work to make the experience smooth overall.

```bash
# Install
yay -S hyprwhspr

# Or update
yay -Syu hyprwhspr
```

Or switch to bleeding edge:

```bash
yay -S hyprwhspr-git
```

## What's New

### 🚀 Realtime WebSocket backend

- **Low-latency streaming transcription** via OpenAI's GPT Realtime Mini (2025-12-15) 
- **Two modes available:**
  - `transcribe` - Pure speech-to-text streaming,  3-4x faster than HTTP
  - `converse` - Voice-to-AI conversation mode. Record a prompt, receive an LLM response
- Automatic audio resampling and buffering for optimal performance, just works
- Fast WebSocket reconnection with exponential backoff
- :warning:  Ensure you look into pricing - it's faster, **and** more expensive than transcription endpoints

### New providers

- **OpenAI models:**
  - GPT-4o Mini Transcribe (2025-12-15)

### CLI Improvements

- **`hyprwhspr uninstall`** - Complete removal of hyprwhspr and user data
- **`hyprwhspr backend repair`** - Diagnose and repair corrupted installations
- **`hyprwhspr state reset`** - Reset installation state
- Improved setup UX with cleaner prompts and better error messages
- Better backend selection and switching workflow

### ✨ Polish
- **Mic not ready errors on boot** - It's common for mics to need to be reseated via usb cable on boot/resume. We will now ERR appropriately and give proper guidance via log and tooltip. Once re-seated, RDY state will uptake automatically, and first record will "just work".
- Improved buffer handling for realtime streaming
- Better error messages and logging
- Enhanced boot UX and startup experience
- Cleaner metadata passing and configuration management
- Improved udev device detection
- Faster failure detection and more graceful error handling in general
- New `grab_keys` config key to avoid conflic with other daemons
- Better handling of keyboard ownership if multiple owners

    You may need to update your setup if you use:

    -   **Node.js older than 20.19 or 22.12:** upgrade Node.js, or stay on the previous release of `@linear/sdk`.
    -   **Jest in CommonJS mode:** Jest can't `require()` ES modules. Let `babel-jest` transform the SDK by adding `transformIgnorePatterns: ["/node_modules/(?!@linear/sdk)"]`, or run Jest with native ESM support (`--experimental-vm-modules`).

## World of ClaudeCraft v0.44.0

Version 0.44.0 is the World Quests release. A board of rotating world quests now runs across the
realm on a shared daily calendar, and every quest you finish earns standing with one of three
allied factions, whose quartermasters sell their stock for the currency those quests pay. Around
it sit a weekly emissary and a Weekly Vault, Buried Hoards (treasure maps from the daily board that
open instanced vaults with their own bosses), a trinket slot, and the Viridian Valestrider. World
PvP arrives with an opt-in flag, King of the Hill and a second Warfare season, Thundercall shamans
get a classic elemental rework, scheduled ferries sail between rebuilt harbors, and the interface
gains a Cooldown Manager, frame presets and a death recap. This release also carries everything
from the v0.43.1 to v0.43.3 hotfix lines, which were forward-merged into it.

### Highlights

- World Quests: a daily board of rotating activities, from caravans and shipwreck salvage to glider
  courses and puzzles, each paying XP, coin, faction standing and faction currency.
- Three allied factions with standing tiers, titles, deeds and quartermasters, a weekly emissary
  charge, and a Weekly Vault that turns a week's activity into a reward you choose.
- Buried Hoards: the day's full board pays a treasure map that opens a vault with its own boss.
- A trinket slot with 18 trinkets, and enemy gear in four permanently stronger qualities.
- World PvP with gold and honor stakes, King of the Hill, and Warfare Season 2 sets for every spec.
- Thundercall is rebuilt around Arc Overload, Magma Burst and Stormbreak.
- Two scheduled passenger ferries, the Cooldown Manager, ten saved frame presets and a death recap.

### World Quests and factions

- **The board.** Taskmaster Kaelen in Eastbrook opens the World Quests board on the map, and you
  may replace one quest a day. Activities include escorting caravans, loading freight, salvaging
  the Farshore shipwreck while rift raiders come for it, holding a cannon line, three glider
  courses, the forge, calligraphy, the ley beam and Confection Cascade puzzles, stealing sealed
  orders under cover of shadow, the Evergarden wisp maze (now a hedge maze) and 39 zone hunts.
  Minigames stay open for practice, though only the first completion each day pays; glider courses
  keep daily and lifetime records on the wharf signboard, and the World Quest Rankings window keeps
  a ladder per medal world quest.
- **Rewards.** Every world quest pays XP, coin (31 silver at level 20), standing with its zone's
  faction (30 up to level 15, then 80, or 100 for the Automatons) and 5 of that faction's currency
  (10 from level 16). From level 16, three zones a day carry an item from your class's table, the
  same three for the whole realm, and a map marker's hover card shows the exact piece.
- **Factions.** The Rift Watch (the coast, from Drifthaven), the Church Order (the heartland, from
  Eastbrook Vale) and the Automatons (the far reaches, from Wyrmwatch) each climb through
  Recognized, Trusted, Proven, Vanguard and Champion, every rung with a faction title; characters
  of level 15 and below pause at Trusted. A new Reputation tab tracks them, a new tier plays a
  banner, and the Champion deeds grant the Riftwarden, Dawnkeeper and Forgemaster titles.
- **Quartermasters.** Quartermaster Vaelen, Templar Althea and Artificer Tobrin sell jewelry, waist
  and feet armor, a pre-raid set piece, proc weapons, bags, toys and recipes for Rift Watch Marks,
  Order Crests and Automaton Cogs: gear costs 15 at Recognized, 35 at Trusted, 75 at Proven, 150 at
  Vanguard and 200 at Champion, and spending never lowers standing. At Proven, four weapon enchant
  formulas for Enchanting 100: Riftwalker's Grace (a chance on hit for 60 Agility and 2% faster
  attacks for 15 sec), Dawnfire (18 Spell Power), Dawn's Benediction (34 Healing Power) and Piston
  Drive for two-handers (12 Strength, 25 crit rating).
- **The Viridian Valestrider**, a teal avian coast-runner with its own animations and 15 recorded
  sounds, is sold for 100 gold from the Rift Watch's Champion stock.
- **The weekly emissary.** Cham Pete in Eastbrook Vale offers four charges (dungeons, the raid,
  battlegrounds or the world boss), one per week. Finishing it pays a purse, an Emissary's Cache (a
  Normal raid piece your class can wear, never a set piece, plus three Heroic Marks) and a
  commendation of 1,000 standing with a faction you pick. The week turns on Tuesday.
- **The Weekly Vault.** A stone hall in Eastbrook, with the Vault Keeper at its door, tracks raid
  encounters, dungeon clears, rated PvP and world quests (2, 4 and 8 turn-ins, drawing on the item
  level 29 Nythraxis Normal loot). Choose the loot tables your rolls use, inspect the candidates
  and claim one item per earned week; an unclaimed week waits without rerolling. Rolls stay within
  three levels above yours, and Warriors, Rogues and Hunters never roll caster stats.

### Buried Hoards

- **Treasure maps.** Clearing every zone slot of the day's board at level 16 or above pays a map:
  common (40 in 100), rare (35), epic (20) or legendary (5). Read it to learn the zone, stand on the
  X and use it again, and a private vault opens for you and your party. Cartographer's Ink (60
  currency at any quartermaster) redraws a read map one rarity finer.
- **The vaults.** Common and rare hoards are caves with four soloable bosses (the Mother of
  Mushrooms, Deeprake, the Colossal Bat, the Voracious Chest); epic and legendary ones are open-air
  rooms with eight themed bosses. A hoard scales to its party, and only ever up for a late joiner.
- **The Coinsack Scurrier.** A 15% chance per hoard of a fleeing goblin: kill it before its 20 sec
  escape portal and every player is paid. A guest is paid for at most three hoards a day.

### PvP

- **The World PvP flag.** /pvp (or the World PvP tab on G) raises it from level 10; lowering takes
  5 minutes and waits out combat. Proving Shore and Eastbrook Vale are sanctuaries; the Drakelands,
  the Frostveil Reach and the Amberfall are free-for-all; elsewhere both players must be flagged.
  Party, raid and guild mates are never hostile.
- **Stakes.** A kill pays a 10 Honor pool and moves min(5 gold, 10% of a flagged victim's purse),
  split between the killing blow, everyone who hit the victim in the last 10 sec and the flagged
  healers who kept them up. Repeat kills of one victim pay 100, 50, 25, then 0 percent for an hour,
  and a victim more than 5 levels below you pays nothing.
- **King of the Hill.** Once every three hours the realm gets 15 minutes' warning of a 50-yard
  circle in a free-for-all zone, which stands for 45 minutes. The party with the most members
  inside takes it after 60 sec of unbroken majority, and each holder inside earns 2 Honor a minute,
  climbing to 12 the longer the party holds: about 380 each for a full uncontested stand.
- **Warfare Season 2: Vanguard.** 27 class-locked five-piece sets, one per spec, with 2-piece and
  4-piece bonuses, plus four weapons, at item level 35: 6,600 Honor a set and 1,800 a weapon, from
  FURY and Warmarshal Draven Kole. Season 1 stays on sale as the entry tier.

### Classes and abilities

- **Thundercall rework.** Earthen Jolt and Faultwake spend any Thunder, not only a full bank. Arc
  Overload (level 10) gives Arc Bolt and Skybranch a 20% chance to strike again for half damage and
  1 Thunder, and Lightning Mastery casts them a third faster (rank-4 Arc Bolt 3.0 to 2.0 sec).
  Magma Burst (level 12) is a 2.0 sec Fire nuke on an 8 sec cooldown that always crits your Cinder
  Jolt target, and each Cinder Jolt tick has a 20% chance to make it ready and instant for 10 sec.
  Stormbreak (level 16, instant, 45 sec cooldown) slows enemies within 10 yards by 50% and returns
  8% of your mana. The Stormkindled 2-piece raises Arc Overload to 30% and the 4-piece adds 20% to
  Magma Burst; with the full set the spec benches 259.0 DPS on Ignivar, up from 227.2.
- **Feral.** Melee reaches 1 yard further, Slinkstrike and Lunge bank Old Blood, and Stalk, Lunge
  and Bruin Rush take you into their form (Lunge reaches 25 yards; both gap closers are off the
  global cooldown). Nature's Boon gives a landed auto-attack a 1 in 15 chance to make Wildbloom (or
  Oakhide in Bruin Form) free, 25% stronger and castable in form for 10 sec. Oakhide is +20% armor
  (30% with Oakhide Reflex) instead of a flat 150, and Dash takes Cat Form to 172.5% (was 150%).
- **Tank threat.** Oathward raises threat by 100% (was 40%) and Recompense by 110% (was 80%): live
  raid parses had the Faithwarden at a median 234 threat per second against the Ironguard's 330.
- **Dawnreaver.** Final Edict and Dawnfall deal 2.0 times their damage, Tolling Hammer 1.75 times
  and Verdict of the Sun God 1.5 times, taking a 120 sec heroic dummy from 213.6 to 313.0 DPS.
- **Holy priest.** Choirmend has a 12 sec cooldown. In the redesigned Benison Dawnweave set each
  Whispered, Solemn or Urgent Prayer adds 10% to your next Choirmend (up to 3 stacks), and three
  stacks make your next Whispered Prayer instant and 100% stronger within 60 sec.
- **Warrior** abilities gain authored animations, impacts, shouts and spatial audio, and Red
  Harvest lands 0.5 sec after the press. **Chronomancer** Echo healing scales with Healing Power.
  Moonwing Form grows antlers, a crescent and moth wings, and Gloamveil veils the priest's face.
- **Exploits closed.** A talent swap removes the buffs only the dropped talent could give (no more
  two capstones), re-entering Cat Form mid-fight returns the energy you had instead of a full bar,
  Double Blink no longer fires in bursts after Winter's Recall, and a gear swap no longer refunds
  frost's second Cold Coffin charge.
- **Also:** Recall the Fallen finds a fallen group member without a selected corpse, Solar
  Invocation follows a party-frame mouseover, Trailbreak's leap clears rising ground, and Leaden Hex
  no longer pulls a mob before the bolt lands. Stonebound Weapon draws a solid sheath on Low.

### Raids and dungeons

- **Heroic Crucible loot.** Every Heroic kill of Ignivar and Varkhul pays a guaranteed Robe sigil
  beside a gear slot Normal lacks, three items per 10-player kill against two, and the Wand of
  Quenched Sparks, the Orb of the Last Spring and the Cinder of the First Design move to Heroic.
- **Nythraxis.** Bone Storm releases live Soul Rend marks unresolved and waits 6 sec after a
  detonation, so the raid is never asked to stack and scatter at once, and it clears Dread Curse,
  whose stacks could push a Heroic Bone Slam past 100% of the tank's health. The Grave Eruption
  warning gains a thick rim, and Colorblind Mode (Options, Interface) moves every Nythraxis floor
  hazard onto a colorblind-safe palette without changing its size or timing.
- **Boss telegraphs always paint over player ground effects** such as a consecration or frost ring.
- **Loot and resets.** A raider who released at the back of the room shares the kill, so lockout
  and loot rights always land together; a wiped boss resets fully even if someone zones in on the
  wipe tick; raids switch Normal and Heroic without the 5 minute cooldown; and Heroic clears count
  on the Reliquary pages of the five-man dungeons and Nythraxis.

### World and travel

- **Ferries.** A three-masted ship with a walkable deck sails two free timetabled routes: Eastbrook
  to a new pier at Moonrest in the Nightbloom, and Wickharbor in the Galecrest to a cliff harbor
  below Wyrmwatch, where Harbormaster Tamsin keeps a walk-in house. The HUD shows the next
  departure, signposts mark every berth, and four crossings earn the Harbor to Harbor deed.
- **Death.** The Keeper's Toll revive now comes from talking to the Pale Keeper, with a confirmation
  that states the cost, and a ghost sees a line naming both roads back. A resurrection in place
  keeps your heading, and a ghost can use the Duskfall passage out of the Veiled Hollow.
- **The first /unstuck in an hour is free**; a repeat within the hour charges Unstuck Sickness.
  Leaving a dungeon or a Rift faces you away from the door, and a Thornpeak hillside pocket that
  trapped players is regraded.

### Interface and options

- **Frame presets.** Save up to ten named layouts with UI scale (75% to 200%), positions, sizes,
  visibility and grouping, and import or export them. Three movable focus frames, a movable Target
  of Target frame and a grouped Show/Hide Frames menu come with it, and layouts no longer reset.
- **Cooldown Manager** (Options, Overlays): up to twelve groups of floating buttons that show a
  spell's cooldown, dim while it cannot be cast, and light and chime when it is ready.
- **The unit tooltip moves** (Edit Frames) and shows a player's title, guild and spec with role.
- **Meters and death recap.** Meter rows carry spec icons and a customization dialog, a Recap button
  beside Release Spirit lists every hit, heal and absorb before your death, and absorbs now count
  as the shielder's healing.
- **Character sheet.** A footer tab strip with Reputation, Currencies and Progression, the spec
  picker moves to the talent window, and the stats add Healing Power and Spell Crit.
- **Action bar.** Abilities grey out while a requirement is unmet: an execute above 20% health, a
  finisher with no combo points, a stealth in combat, a form ability out of form.
- **More options.** Show Aura Caster in Tooltips, Target Auras Below the Frame, an Action Cam with a
  shoulder slider, the mouseover casting switch at the top of Interface, Frames, a close button on
  Target Auras, and a collapsible world map rail. Other players' faces show in their portraits.

### Items and economy

- **The trinket slot.** Every class gains a trinket slot and 18 trinkets (item level 26 to 35), each
  with one attribute and an on-use effect: heroic five-man bosses, Heroic Nythraxis, Rift clears,
  the Heroic Quartermaster (16 Heroic Marks), the honor vendors (800 Honor) and the Crucible.
- **Exceptional drop qualities.** Eligible uncommon-or-better gear from enemies can drop permanently
  stronger: Superior (9%, +2 item levels), Exceptional (0.9%, +4), Magnificent (0.09%, +6) or
  Transcendent (0.01%, +8). Quest rewards, vendor goods and crafted items never roll it.
- **The Wanted board.** Post World Market buy orders with the gold escrowed (six per character, up
  to 200 units each), filled from the book at or under your price, then by gatherers' deliveries;
  a strip lists every material with no listing at all.
- **Market and trade.** Buy part of a bulk listing, read your sales on a History tab, browse the
  $WOC Exchange from character select, and offer or remove trade items by quantity. A won roll gets
  a gold banner, and full bags a red warning that the item waits on the corpse.
- **Materials Vault and crafting.** The vault gains a name search and deposits a locked stack as
  one row. A placed Grand Cauldron, Laden Hearth or Master's Field Forge now stands in the world,
  apex feasts set out from the bags, and a queued Town Focus re-spec survives a logout.

### Accounts and social

- **Custom guild ranks.** A Ranks tab in the Social window: up to 10 ranks with their own Invite,
  Remove, Promote, Guild Bank, Officer Chat, Billboard and Calendar permissions.
- **Character select** lists each character's raid, dungeon and world boss lockouts. Contributors
  can wear their developer badge rung as a title, Discord can be relinked in place, and the Discord
  rare-drop card names the player who actually won the roll.

### Performance

- **Frame Rate Limit** (Options, System): Auto, Display, 60 or 30. On an Intel Iris Xe at Medium a
  limit of 30 cut the renderer's main-thread time from 664 ms to 295 ms a second.
- **Windows shader compiles.** Lit materials compile in 53 s instead of 102 s over a full Ultra
  tour on an RTX 3060, and Low and Medium ghost blocking buildings with a dithered fade that needs
  no extra shaders (the Camera Ghost dial in Advanced).
- **Freezes removed.** On an Intel HD 530 the first Warrior you meet costs a 107 to 108 ms frame
  instead of 533 to 635 ms, cast effects no longer wait 12 to 20 sec after loading, and the Ignivar
  encounters warm up during the Forge-Lift ride. The first dive, the first rain, class effects, the
  King of the Hill ring, weapon skins and the Goblin Rocket Sled plume no longer compile mid-play.
- **Lighter assets.** 40 scatter props drop from 232,621 to 93,057 triangles (24.0 MB to 10.7 MB).
- **Server and network.** Guild bank autosaves no longer queue behind the World Market, one cause
  of realm-wide lag spikes. Delves predict your movement locally, removing a 0.2 to 0.3 sec input
  delay, and a new target no longer bounces back to the old one online.

### Mobile and desktop

- **System Report** (desktop app, Options, Performance): one button saves a file describing your
  machine's settings to share when asking for help; nothing is uploaded.
- **Touch.** A bag stack can be destroyed again (drag it out, or the new Destroy row), target auras
  hang below the target frame, and the $WOC Exchange browse table fits a portrait phone.

### Fixes

- Dragging from the spellbook or the paperdoll no longer breaks every later drag until a reload,
  all five combo pips show on the player frame, and a deed-bordered name clears the portrait.
- Distant NPCs no longer turn flat and untextured, the Broodmother Egg can be killed again, and Tab
  picks idle mobs only within 20 yards (engaged mobs and hostile players keep the 40-yard reach).
- The key-binding prompt no longer covers the bars, and a map label no longer hides under a badge.

### Compatibility and upgrade notes

- **Free-for-all ground.** The Drakelands, the Frostveil Reach and the Amberfall are hostile to
  everyone present, flag or no flag, apart from party, raid and guild mates. An unflagged player
  killed there loses no gold.
- **Update before you play.** The world layout changed (the new harbors, the Farshore shipwreck and
  the vault hall), so a client from before this release is turned away until it updates.
- **Class changes to plan around.** Choirmend now has a cooldown, the Stormkindled 2-piece no longer
  grants Thunder from Unleash Weapon, and Oakhide is a percentage.
- **Options.** The Specialization tab is gone (pick your spec in the talent window), the Shader
  Warm-up Worker row is withdrawn, and the desktop Performance Overlay entry is now Performance.

### Release plumbing

Version surfaces move to 0.44.0 (Android versionCode 62, iOS build 69). Every new English string
added this cycle is filled across all supported locales, and the wiki seed is regenerated to match.

## World of ClaudeCraft v0.43.0

The interface release: every HUD frame and window is rebuilt on one shared library while keeping the classic look. Around that, the Book of Deeds and the Reliquary become account-wide, every item of uncommon quality and above carries a stamina baseline so casters stop being made of paper, the druid's feral form gets its own authored cat and a real mobility kit, Nythraxis's Bone Storm is retuned from live parses, the World Market learns to buy across many listings at once, and a long run of performance work targets integrated GPUs and four-core laptops. This release also carries everything from the v0.42.1 and v0.42.2 hotfix lines, forward-merged into it.

### Interface

- **The interface is rebuilt on one token and primitive library.** Same classic gold, warm borders, panel gradient, Cinzel titles and painted art, now with one grammar for panels, buttons, tabs, sockets, bars and inputs. Unbacked action bars, a quiet XP rail twelve sockets wide, plateless unit frames with portrait medals and cast ribbons, party panels with a remembered Party N disclosure, and the Talking Head for an NPC line spoken off screen. Every window, from character and bags to the World Market and the dungeon finder, adopts the same shell with every row and control kept.
- **Watched Spells.** Give any known self-buff its own aura overlay, with the full customization set, plus four independent notification channels: an Alert Sound with 20 cues, a Hotbar Glow on the spell's own button, a Reticle Tick, and gamepad Rumble. All default to off.
- **Action bars are remembered per specialization**, and swapping a talent for its alternative on the same choice row puts the new ability in the slot the old one vacated.
- **Hide Interface (Alt+Z)** hides every HUD surface for clean screenshots and videos; Escape always brings it back first.
- **Toggle Friendly Nameplates (Ctrl+V)** hides town NPCs, vendors, quest givers and friendly pets while leaving the enemies you are fighting readable.
- **Party target hotkeys.** Target Self on F1 and Target Party Member 1 to 9 on F2 to F10, rebindable, keyed to the rows you see in the party frames.
- **The mouse wheel binds like a key**, chords included, and camera zoom becomes an ordinary rebindable action.
- **Unlock Interface leads the Esc game menu**, and the map zooms out of an instance plan to the zone map.
- **Raid markers show on the target frame**, and the absorb hatch covers only the shield segment instead of striping the whole health bar.
- **The leaderboard is a ledger** with a podium on every tab and a Your Standing pill, and the combat meters finally count damage dealt to players in duels, arena and battlegrounds.
- **Enter confirms again** after a mouse click opens a dialog, and a new Confirm Sales From Quality setting sells anything below a chosen quality in one click.

### Classes and abilities

- **Cat Form has its own cat.** The druid's feral form is Cat Form in name and body, with an authored quadruped replacing the tinted wolf, a full clip set, and a frame a fifth bigger than a world wolf.
- **Cat Form mobility.** 15% passive speed, Fleet Form breaks breakable roots and slows on cast as a baseline, and Dash is learned at 12 instead of 18.
- **Wildfang kit pass 2.** Loping Stride is baseline on every shift (60% for 3 sec, once per 20 sec) and row 5 becomes Longstride. Pin gives a 3 sec window after Bruin Rush where Cat Form is free and pins the target (50% slow for 4 sec). Stalk moves at full speed, Lunge is the out-of-stealth Slinkstrike, and Hamstring Bite stuns for 0.5 sec plus 0.5 sec per combo point.
- **Chronomancer rework.** Excess healing from Temporal Echo becomes a Temporal Aegis absorb capped at 20% of maximum health, Temporal Cascade reaches 5 targets, and Aether Darts deal 20% more damage under Perfect Moment. Chronomancy buffs also show on the aura tracks for the first time.
- **Warlock.** Possess the Evil Eye and Hour of Judgment no longer need an enemy carrying the primary Evil Eye.
- **A cast you cannot make is refused, not eaten.** Pressing a cast-time or channelled spell while already holding movement is denied with a toast instead of arming the global cooldown for nothing.
- **Rogue poisons** stop reapplying after a duel ends, are attributed to the right rogue in parses, and Festering Venom tooltips stop rounding away Knifework's per-stack damage.

### Raids and dungeons

- **Nythraxis's Bone Storm.** The mid-storm Bone Spike is retired (its counter contradicted the storm's), and the storm's first landed Bone Slam drops to 23% of maximum health on Normal and 37% on Heroic. Later slams keep 35% and 55%.
- **Dread Curse cannot be faked away.** The boss refuses to settle back onto a raider still carrying a live stack while the raider who took it over is clean, so a decoy taunt no longer defeats the swap.
- **The Dungeon Finder catalogues two more.** The Crucible of the Last Spring raid (Ignivar, then Varkhul) as a 10-player Normal and Heroic raid on a weekly lockout, and The Wildheart Basin as a level-cap five-man on Normal and Heroic.
- **Your pet stops body-pulling bosses** from its own proximity scan, while every deliberate order still engages.
- **Heroic loot previews** no longer head a chance-only row with "one of these always drops".
- **Line of sight** is no longer blocked by invisible floor clutter on rift and delve floors.

### World and quests

- **Eastbrook's first-quest handoff.** The starter givers are spaced around the civic square with Marshal Redbrook beside the noticeboard, and the ferry offers optional golden guidance (a glow on the giver and a trail to the objective) to any character who has not finished Wolves at the Door. Profession trainers carry a subtitle, and profession onboarding quests no longer paint markers on nameplates or the map.
- **NPC nameplates say what an NPC does**, from Armor Vendor and Banker to Stable Master and the profession trainers, so a new player can read a town at a glance.
- **Four sunken quest pickups are back on dry land**, including the Bridgemere toll-chest that stuck Toll and Tangle at 2 of 3.
- **The Last Keep churchyard is a real graveyard**, 41 yards from the keep door instead of a 300 yard walk back from the Wyrmwatch cairns.

### Professions and crafting

- **Farming tools.** An unearned land tool degrades to the tier your skill allows instead of vanishing, so upgrading a hoe no longer bricks farming; hoes align to the crop bands they unlock, and planting is instant.
- **Harvesting works from the interact key** for a Field Kit carrier, so keyboard, gamepad and mobile players can reach it again.
- **A fine-only reagent explains itself** when you are holding the plain grade, on the line, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.
- **Charm recipes cost 1 Chime Shard, 14 Chime Essence and 10 Chime Dust** instead of 5, 4 and 6, so a charm takes one epic disenchant rather than five.
- **Pin a recipe** (up to five per character) to an always-on Recipes tracker showing carried and needed counts while you farm.

### Items and economy

- **Health, rebuilt.** Every item of uncommon quality and above carries a stamina baseline of a third of its primary-stat budget, every class gains 2 Stamina per level, and cloth classes plus priest gain 15 health per level.
- **Market Sweep** buys a wanted quantity of one item across many sellers in one command, cheapest per unit first, quoted live before you commit.
- **Sales History** joins the $WOC Exchange as a fourth tab: every completed realm sale with item, seller, buyer, sold-at, price and sale type.
- **The Materials Vault packs one row per material**, with exact-source pickers on desktop right-click and bag-stack steppers on every quantity prompt.
- **A full-bags award waits five minutes** on the corpse instead of decaying after about a minute.
- **Letters age out on a read and unread model** (30 sim-days unread, 90 for Exchange Broker notices, 3 after reading), and anything holding real escrow is never destroyed by age. Signed potions now stack into one mail parcel.
- **Riftbound bands take ring enchants** at every rung, and an offhand weapon finally wears its Armory skin.
- **Try a mount skin before you buy it**, seated on your own character, with Preview added to the Cosmetics window.

### Accounts and social

- **The Book of Deeds and the Reliquary are account-wide**, with Earned by and Found by naming which of your characters got there and when, and deed titles and borders wearable on every character.
- **/who becomes a Who tab** in the Social window: server-side search by name, zone or guild, sorting by any column, a class chip, and guild names the chat dump never carried.
- **The guild signpost** gains a New player friendly category and a green dot for guilds with an officer online right now.
- **Guild gold movements are announced** to every online member the moment an officer deposits or withdraws.
- **Character select shows each character's zone**, resolved through the same rule that places the save on login.

### Performance

- **The HUD stops re-styling itself every frame**, which cost 6.5 ms per frame (31% of the frame) on a four-core Intel HD 530.
- **Lighter forest trunks, per-cell Willowfen culling and gather node batches that stop drawing past the scenery reach**, with no change to what you can see or reach.
- **The renderer stops walking every character rig for raid telegraphs outside an encounter**, stops sampling terrain under every remote body each frame, and stops running readouts nothing is watching.
- **The governor stops mistaking a GPU-bound frame for a 30 Hz display**, so integrated-GPU players get the relief it exists to provide.
- **The shader corpus record is spread across background units** instead of one long freeze, and the Wildheart caldera no longer relinks every material drawn after a visit (the "everything freezes after I die" report).

### Mobile and desktop

- **Desktop and native API calls reach the server again**, so the Arena and Battleground all-time ladders load in the desktop, Android and iOS clients.
- **The class engine indicators drag with one finger on touch** again, and a spot parked before they joined the Unlock Interface registry comes back.
- **Crafting reagent text is legible on a phone**, and long-press tooltips survive finger jitter on iOS.

### Compatibility

- **Frames are locked by default this patch**; Unlock Interface is the first row of the Esc menu. Frame widths are re-stamped, so a custom-dragged frame comes back narrower until you drag it again.
- **Deeds, relics and health change on first login**: both books read your whole account, and the stamina baseline plus the class table raise your health.
- **Stored state is re-read once**: a single saved action bar layout seeds the active spec, vault rows fold to one row per material, and mail countdowns move to the new clocks (only ever shortened). A character already at the first profession tier through gathering alone gets the profession explainer once.
- **Update your app** for the desktop, Android and iOS ladder fix.

## World of ClaudeCraft v0.42.2

A hotfix release on top of v0.42.1: the Nythraxis raid finale reworked from live heroic feedback, and a fix for the Last Flame's Zeal weapon enchant stacking on dual-wielders.

### Nythraxis, Scourge of Thornpeak

- **Soulfire and Gravefire are retired from play.** A Soul Rend detonation still splits its hit across the stacked marks, but leaves no pool on either difficulty, and the Gravefire line is gone with it. The raid guide, the finder chips, and the Raid Boss Guide rows are updated.
- **Bone Spike per-raider cooldown.** No Bone Spike cast, cadence or mid-storm, may pick a raider impaled within the last 55 seconds, measured from the impale on the encounter clock, so consecutive waves spread across the raid instead of landing on the same player.
- **Bone Spikes are wards.** A spike now takes 4 hits on Normal and 6 on Heroic, from anyone, each landed hit counting one whatever it deals; its health bar reads as hits remaining.
- **Bone Spikes read as ember orange** on every graphics tier, so they no longer blend into the bone golem or the flagstone floor.
- **The Binding Sigil stands on two platforms** flanking the throne, 30 yards to the raid's left or right of where the boss spawned, alternating each cast. A Normal-mode fire crossover remembers the side the sigil actually landed on, and ward hits keep their original-attack provenance for Crafted Momentum.

### Enchants

- **Last Flame's Zeal is one shared buff.** The 50 Strength proc is keyed by the enchant rather than by the striking hand, so a dual-wielder with both weapons enchanted can no longer stack two copies. A trigger from either hand refreshes the one buff, and it never stacks. Tooltip and guide text say so in every language.

### Release plumbing

Version surfaces move to 0.42.2 (Android versionCode 57, iOS build 64). The Fenbridge asset fingerprints were re-minted for the version bump.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.42.0

**Released:** 2026-09-09  
**Previous release:** v0.41.4

Version 0.42.0 is the largest release in the game's history: 2,512 commits across roughly 120
pull requests since v0.41.4. It ships the Masterwrought crafting endgame with the farming
profession and deliberate gathering, rebuilds Nythraxis as a three-phase movement fight, redraws
the Drakelands, puts every instance on one loot cadence, adds the Rift Forge, rebalances thirteen
specializations, makes every HUD surface a movable frame, sells the first account-wide mount skins,
and lands a broad rendering performance program alongside complete translations in all 21 locales.

## Highlights

- Craft the Masterwrought apex tier in every profession, take a piece through four ranks of
  Perfecting, and promote it to a named legendary; farm eight crops across sessions; harvest
  corpses deliberately with a Field Kit; track a recipe or commission with a live material
  checklist.
- Face the rebuilt Nythraxis, Scourge of Thornpeak, on Normal and Heroic, with Roots' Bramblehide
  and seven gap-fill drops on his table, and walk the redrawn Drakelands where the Last Keep and
  Wyrmwatch are rebuilt from a new kit.
- Every raid and heroic dungeon boss now pays one item per five intended players per kill, instance
  boss corpses stay lootable for thirty minutes, and Riftbound bands sit on an item-level ladder
  with gem sockets at the new Rift Forge.
- Thirteen specializations are rebalanced from measured simulation: about 10 percent more damage
  for Wildfang, Thundercall, Fieldcraft, Ruination, Knifework, and Coldsight, a Necromancy rework,
  Skulduggery's stealth opener, Dirge power scaling for Vespers, Groveheart's corrected replants,
  and healing lifts for Spiritcall, Sunmender, and Doctrine.
- Move every standing HUD surface, track your own buffs on six opt-in aura tracks and your dots on
  a Target Dots frame and enemy nameplates, export and import your whole key map and settings, see
  a live keyboard overview, and keep separate action-bar layouts for desktop and touch.
- Wear five new account-wide mount skins over any mount, buy guild roster pages for gold, page
  through a searchable guild bank history, get a Discord DM when a battleground or arena queue
  pops, and browse every loot source in the Loot Explorer.
- Play with far fewer shader stalls (a warm-up worker on Windows, Vulkan on the Linux desktop app)
  and a cheaper frame everywhere: merged character rigs, tiered shadows, foliage, VFX, and
  post-processing, and black-frame and context-loss fixes on Android and WebGL.
- Play with complete v0.42.0 translations across every shipped locale.

## Masterwrought crafting, farming, and gathering

The crafting endgame arrives as the Masterwrought apex tier across all ten crafts. Apex recipes
are learned from tradable pattern items dropped by raids, won from rift clears, or sold by the
Heroic Quartermaster. Maker's Embers are earned weekly and bank when missed, Wyrmfall Cores come
from raid boss kills and daily rift first clears, and Sundered Essence comes from breaking down
raid-won epics. A character can wear two Masterwrought pieces at once, at most one of them
legendary.

- Perfecting (Shift+T) takes an apex piece through four ranks at an 80 percent success chance per
  attempt. Every attempt, success or fail, consumes one Maker's Ember, one Sundered Essence, and
  one Prismglass Setting, and is self-service at skill 125 in the craft that made the piece.
- A Perfected piece can be promoted to legendary presentation for one Deed of Making and a chosen
  name. The promotion is cosmetic and deterministic: orange identity, no extra stats.
- Every crafted or gathered stack carries its maker's provenance through crafting, trade, mail,
  and storage, and a free Perfecting rank exchange moves progress between two owned copies of the
  same collection piece (both copies bind).
- Any existing enchant, including the identical one, can be overwritten after a confirmation that
  names the old and new enchant and the reagent cost; the full reagents are consumed and normal
  Enchanting skill progress applies, so gear you intend to keep can still train the craft.
- Jewelcrafting and Inscription gain trainer-taught base catalogs (nine forge-bound jewelcrafting
  recipes; six inscription recipes of caster tomes and buff scrolls), and held inscription tomes
  are the first visible held off-hands.

Crucible crafted collections give raiders eleven role-specific armor collections (chest, waist,
and feet, 33 pieces) with a bonus at any two pieces from one collection, at item level 35 and 38
once Perfected, inside the same two-piece equip cap. Collection manuals teach all three recipes at
once and, like the Last Flame's Zeal weapon-enchant formula, come from Crucible drops or the raid's
Core vendor; each piece costs three undiscounted Cores of the Last Flame plus ordinary materials,
with no daily craft gate. Last Flame's Zeal grants 50 Strength for 15 seconds plus 200
self-healing at about one proc per minute. Across the tested offensive profiles, mixed two-piece
sets measured 3.4 to 13.1 percent above the old six-piece raid sets.

The Forgefather legendary hammer is a personal chain: Forgefather's Ember drops from Varkhul on
Normal or Heroic, using it finishes the recovery quest, teaches the one-use recipe, and starts
Requiem at the Forge; shaping Forgebreaker at Weaponcrafting 125 consumes the Ember, 15 Cores of
the Last Flame, 10 Fine Osmium Ore, and 6 Fine Highpine Logs, and a failed or cancelled craft keeps
both. The hammer is item level 55, soulbound, outside the Masterwrought cap and Perfecting, and
cannot be commissioned. The three Crucible lore quests and both hammer quests now reward 5,300 XP
and 2 gold 50 silver each.

Farming joins mining, logging, herbalism, and fishing as the fifth gathering profession, and it is
the first that pays out across sessions: plant a bed with a hoe, leave, come back to harvest. Four
Farmer NPCs seat the profession and open its intro quest, eight crops (with fine twins) grow in
tiered patches behind a five-rung hoe ladder, compost, growth tonic, husk trades, and seed-back
rolls round out the loop, and produce feeds cooking and alchemy only (eight plain farm dishes per
crop tier, four Well Fed buff dishes, and shared feasts). Growth is wall-clock gated, so farming
skill climbs slowest of the five trades, and the read-only Harvest Journal (Shift+K) lists every
planted bed and the time left on it.

Gathering is deliberate now. Interact on a corpse takes only ordinary loot; profession materials
need a reusable Field Kit (20 copper from general quartermasters and gathering vendors) and an
explicit Harvest action with a 1.5-second cast. The killer's party holds harvest priority for ten
seconds, then the body opens to the first eligible harvester. Harvesting can start the moment a kill
lands and continues while combat is active; damage, movement, and death still interrupt it. One
preference picker (from the kit, the Professions window, or a corpse) chooses all materials or one
specific material, and the Harvest button no longer flashes or reports a false "Unavailable
material" while its availability poll is pending.

- Compatible material units gathered by different players share one real stack while keeping
  exact per-contributor counts, with a Sources view, split by gatherer, and recombine.
- Players track one recipe or one accepted commission at a time with a chosen quantity and a live
  checklist of carried, stored, missing, and usable-now materials. A Sources panel on every
  tracked ingredient discloses which creatures, zones, tools, skills, crop timers, and fishing spots
  supply it, derived from the shipped content.
- Materials-only satchels show both pools honestly ("Items 16/16, Materials 1/8"), the
  Materials Vault Deposit All sweep names the first epic-or-better material it moves, crafting
  spends the exact pattern copy you clicked, and usable quest items show a use hint.

## Nythraxis and the Drakelands

Nythraxis, Scourge of Thornpeak, is rebuilt as a three-phase movement fight on both Normal and
Heroic. Dread Curse forces a tank swap every phase, Bone Spikes impale raiders, Grave Eruption
leaves burning ground, and Binding Sigils must be dragged under the boss to interrupt Deathless
Ascension. At 70 percent the wardstones and Brother Aldric join and Soul Rend forces the raid to
stack and then scatter out of the resulting Soulfire; at 30 percent The King's Wrath brings Bone
Storm charges, Bone Slams, and the hard enrage The Crown Endures. Summoned add waves are off by
design. Nythraxis has 120,000 health on Normal and 192,000 on Heroic, his melee lands at about 90
percent of his Crucible counterpart's swing on each difficulty (Normal Ignivar, Heroic Varkhul),
and Heroic fire now burns out (Grave Flame 8 seconds, Soulfire 12 seconds) instead of filling the
room. The Dungeon Finder guidance and a solo practice raid for developers ship alongside it.

The Drakelands receive their full map improvements pass. The Last Keep castle and the Ashen Bulwark
are gone; the keep and the Trollmoot swap sites, and the keep and Wyrmwatch are rebuilt from a new
twenty-piece kit across seven placement passes (walls, temple court, training yard, plazas,
boardwalk, barracks, chapel and churchyard, Wyrmwatch's tavern row, stables, church, and well).
Standable plates now carry pass-under heights, stairs walk in both directions, a mounted rider can
cross the strait bridge, the slope glue can no longer seat a walker below the terrain where a
standable prop dips under rising ground, and the Forge-Lift car's side panels are solid so riders
no longer wedge in its corners. The Forgefather's Isle sea-ring parapet no longer clips through its
northwest wall.

## Loot, the Rift Forge, and the Reliquary

Instance equipment now follows one cadence: one item per five intended players per boss kill.

- Nythraxis pays two gear items per kill on either difficulty (down from five to seven on Normal
  and six to eight on Heroic). Every existing item stays obtainable at proportional weight, and
  Deathless Heartwood and Kingsbane keep their 3 percent chance each but share one slot.
- Ten named heroic dungeon bosses pay one gear item each from a single combined Heroic partition.
- Ignivar and Varkhul pay two items per kill on both difficulties (down from four on Normal and six
  to seven on Heroic). Slot one is the boss's merged sigil partition; slot two is a Normal-only
  off-set partition or a Heroic-only exclusive partition. Hit gear (waists, necks, rings) drops on
  Normal only, so a Heroic roster still needs Normal clears to cap hit.
- Roots' Bramblehide, a seven-piece Wildfang leather set at item level 29 (33 on Heroic claim),
  joins the Nythraxis Normal table, along with seven gap-fill drops for previously empty slots:
  Courtier's Bonefang, Thornpeak Wardblade, Gravecourt Hewer, Votive Ward of the Deathless Court,
  Thornpeak Moonhide Cowl, Stormhymn Chain Grips, and Stormhymn Chain Treads.
- Heroic Varkhul's three intermission add pools are retuned to 0.7x health (88,500 total to
  61,950); timers, wave count, forge heat, beams, and the meltdown enrage are unchanged.
- Instance bosses (raids, dungeons, rift floors, delves) hold a lootable corpse for thirty minutes
  instead of the sixty-second trash window that had been applying to them.
- A full-bags roll award is held on the corpse for the winner to claim once they have room.
- The Drowned Litany and Collapsed Reliquary Bountiful Coffer rates rise from 5 and 2 percent to
  20 and 8 percent (Heroic and Normal), and the epic inside a coffer from 3 to 12 percent.

Riftbound bands sit on an item-level ladder: rank C 20, B 23, A 26, S 29, plus one item level per
Rift Essence upgrade, capped at 34 (one below the Ignivar raid ring line). Gem sockets (crimson
crit, azure haste, verdant hit, 12 rating each) replace the old forge enchant. Riftwright Maelis,
a new NPC in the Watch Meadow on the Farshore, runs the Rift Forge window where bands are upgraded
and socketed. Every existing band re-prices onto the ladder the first time it loads.

The Loot Explorer is a new searchable, filterable catalog of every item and where it comes from
(open world, dungeon, raid, delve, rift, vendor stock, quest rewards, ground pickups, and class
starting gear), browsable by item or by encounter, opened with Shift+O, the minimap chest icon, or
the mobile More tray. The Reliquary shelf gains an All / Illuminated / Remaining chip, relic
tooltips name their vendor unlock gate, and the retired Fiesta bracket and Vale Cup deeds move to
Feats of Strength so the Whole Book capstone is no longer stranded. The Realm Builder of the Month
monument replaces Eastbrook Vale's civic well beacon: a builder statue whose plates carry the
current honouree's name, named each month from the new Realm Builders page in the admin dashboard.

## Graphics, audio, and performance

- Shader stalls fall on every platform: fewer program links everywhere; on Windows a shader
  warm-up worker pre-links the exact programs the renderer is about to use, taking heavy links from
  315 to 689 ms down to 50 to 117 ms; and the Linux desktop app switches to the Vulkan backend,
  where a cold link costs about a tenth of OpenGL, with an AMD workaround and a bounded fallback
  ladder so nothing strands a player on a loading screen.
- Composed character rigs share one skeleton and one merged body instead of about twenty skeletons
  and nine draws each, rigs are frustum-culled per pass, and static prop shadow casters merge with
  their non-casters.
- The sun shadow pass renders High at a 2560 map instead of 4096 and sheds coverage under
  sustained load to a 67-yard floor; blade grass culls and uploads sector by sector; zone
  dressing, foliage density, tree draw distance, canopy detail, and texture anisotropy all gain
  real per-tier ladders.
- Ability and weapon VFX cost less per slot, the post-processing chain is budgeted by real
  drawing-buffer pixels (1440p and 4K stop paying for full-resolution ambient occlusion), three
  wasted full-screen compositor surfaces are gone, and two governed budget levels (terrain detail
  and a post-processing shed that steps SMAA to FXAA and trims bloom) engage under pressure.
- Every one of these knobs is classified cosmetic-only under the graphics-settings fairness rule:
  no tier hides anything a player acts on, and collider-backed dressing stays whole at every tier.
- Android Mali panels no longer render black frames from a NaN in the ambient-occlusion upsample;
  a WebGL context loss that never restores now prompts a reload; a graphics preset switch disposes
  terrain, far-vista, and water views and bounds the KTX2 restore wait at three seconds instead of
  minutes; Low-tier rocks and dressing stay visible as the camera orbits; Lambert terrain stops
  going black on slopes at dusk; and eighteen creature and mount rigs with authored atlases lose
  the grey emissive film that washed them out.
- Held inscription tomes are the first visible held off-hands, promoted legendary gear has an
  orange visual identity, Tripo-generated textures ship as UASTC, the client reports GPU model,
  form factor, adapter, graphics backend, and the real drawing buffer in its performance report,
  and the ?perf overlay shows the post shed rung and render scale.
- Audio: withered crops get their own cue, feast placement has an end-to-end cue chain, the
  player's own footfalls ride the tortoise and troll mounts, the Rallycart's reverse takes and the
  sled's summon take join the manifest, and vehicle engine transitions carry through summon and
  idle handoffs.

## Combat and class balance

Thirteen specializations are retuned in one pass from measured simulation (24 paired seeds, 180
seconds, fixed legal fixtures), with the design, measurements, and results checked in under
`docs/design/class-balance-v042*.md`. These are fixture results, not a live-population forecast.

- Wildfang, Thundercall, Fieldcraft, Ruination, and Knifework gain about 10 percent damage.
- Coldsight gains about 10 percent through a new resource: six completed Fevered Draw pulses grant
  a ten-second Read, spent on an accepted Long Draw for 50 percent more complete-hit damage or on
  Fell Shot for 75 percent more. A rejected cast keeps the Read; an interrupted accepted cast
  spends it.
- Necromancy gains about 20 percent damage.
- Skulduggery trades sustained output for a much stronger true-stealth opener (the first stealth
  strike lands about 55 percent harder, sustained damage falls about 10 percent). Stealth and
  Veiled Edge bonuses no longer stack, and a true-stealth opener preserves an armed Edge.
- Vespers: a successful own-Dirge reapplication refreshes every existing own Dirge on living
  hostile mobs within 30 yards and line of sight, and an omitted Dirge power multiplier is fixed.
  The Gloomtithe bank stays visible past the low-tier buff cap.
- Spiritcall and Sunmender gain 10 percent complete primary healing. Groveheart gains about 20
  percent full-engine healing: Wildbloom replants now carry their Healing Power multipliers and
  match a fresh application, with the primary factor calibrated to 1.05.
- Doctrine gains 30 percent personal spell and wand damage, a 15 percent fallback conversion when
  no eligible injured link exists, and Scouring Mercy now copies to two nearby injured group
  allies for 50 percent of its effective healing each, within 30 yards.
- The Cinderbark and Ruincaller four-piece coefficients are rescaled so they still deliver their
  advertised 30 and 20 percent bonuses over the new baselines.

Chronomancy sustains offensive raid healing without touching its direct heals: individual Temporal
Echoes last 22.5 seconds (from 15), Cascade group Echoes 15 seconds (from 10), Temporal Cascade
casts in 1.5 seconds (from 2.0) and costs 30 percent less mana with Chronoweave 4p, and Aether Surge
and Aether Darts convert 160 percent into Echoes (200 with Chronoweave 2p). Group Echoes are
distributed by missing health, reserving healing for allies below 60 percent, and Temporal
Cascade's own heal scales with each ally's missing health up to four times the authored roll, so it
heals exactly what it always did on a topped-off group and 23 to 158 percent more under real
pressure. In twelve-seed Heroic Ignivar simulations a Chronomancer paired with a Spiritcall shaman
won eleven pulls.

Rogue poisons are real weapon coats. Melting Acid and Nightshade Coating are 30-minute self-cast
coatings applied on every landed melee swing (5 percent armor reduction, and 25 percent less
healing received, 12 seconds each). Festering Venom no longer adds flat swing damage: it stacks a
Nature damage-over-time up to five times (4 per stack every 2 seconds, refreshed to 12 seconds on
every swing), while Adder's Bite rises from 8 to 14 per swing, and Redhanded's poison damage
reaches the coat rider.

- Warlock Possess the Evil Eye and Hour of Judgment fire through a running Needle of Fate cast or
  Consume channel instead of failing with "You are busy."
- A ready wand swing fires between spell-queued casts, restoring wand uptime while mashing a queued
  spell.
- A refused cast (out of range, no resource, on cooldown) no longer leaves a stale auto-attack
  engage armed, so the next unrelated cast such as Soulwell cannot pull you into combat.
- Rune of Power no longer engages auto-attack, Eye Jab resets the rogue's own swing timer so the
  incapacitate is not self-broken, Loping Stride stamps its real move-speed multiplier, pets refuse
  to attack or acquire a mob mid-evade, and knockback no longer freezes a player against a wall at
  zero clearance.
- The self in-combat flag now reaches the client, so the player frame, combat music, and "cannot
  be cast in combat" refusals agree while a boss holds you on its hate table.
- A mouseover combat resurrection reaches a raid member who released and is waiting as a ghost
  outside interest range, while still refusing an ex-member.
- Raid parties switch difficulty without disbanding: the door-entry mismatch notice fires in both
  directions, Reset All Instances covers raid claims and their weekly and daily lockouts, Ignivar's
  linked rooms reset as one occupancy family, and the disband-and-reform bypass is closed.
- In a battleground, Escape then Unstuck resolves a wall-trapped fighter through the live match
  bounds and recovers them to their team graveyard.
- Remote-entity teleport snapping scales its threshold with elapsed time, so mounted players and a
  charging warrior pop less under jittery ping.

## Server, netcode, and telemetry

- A socket that goes silent without a clean close (a WiFi-to-cellular handoff, a router reboot) is
  reaped after ten minutes however late the keepalive sweep runs, so a character is never stuck
  online; the reaped session enters the ordinary linkdead grace and the next reconnect resumes it.
- The Exchange no longer flickers between working and "trading is paused" during a one-print
  price-gate halt: health rides the price cache's 30-second stale-serve bound, so a real sustained
  pause still reaches players within that window.
- Client performance reports gain the GPU model, laptop status, a high-performance adapter
  mismatch flag, the graphics backend (D3D11, Vulkan, Metal, OpenGL), and the real drawing buffer,
  parsed server-side and never self-reported.
- Character saves take the row lock before the fenced live save, the save fence carries an expiry
  qualifier, and the escrow save path is excluded from the lock.
- Guild roster purchases and the Realm Builder honour roll write through fenced transactions,
  queue-notification database work is bounded under outages and large queues, and the name banlist
  is capped at 64 KiB and indexed per screen.

## Compatibility, deploy order, and rollback

This release moves the online world layout epoch (`ONLINE_WORLD_LAYOUT_VERSION` 25 to 29), because
equipped-item snapshots now carry Perfecting fields and the player wire carries the farm-plot delta.
When the server moves, every stale client session is disconnected with an incompatible-version
error and must reload; plan player communications for a hard reload, not for cosmetic skew.

- Deploy the server first, then publish the mobile OTA bundle and let web and desktop clients
  refresh. The mobile update gate turns the incompatible-version refusal into download-then-apply,
  and `scripts/ota/check_server_layout.mjs` is the preflight that proves the running server speaks
  the bundle's layout (`docs/ota-updates.md`).
- Deploy the first boot with every realm stopped, like any seeding boot. The audit-growth budget
  (`BANK_LEDGER_GROWTH_HARD_LIMIT_ROWS`, default still 10,000,000) becomes one aggregate, net
  ceiling over `bank_ledger` plus `material_source_journal`, and the first boot of this release runs
  a one-time converging migration inside the schema boot transaction: it adds two columns,
  publishes three triggers, locks both counted tables, and replaces the committed count with an
  exact recount over the real ledger history. A realm left running during that boot stalls its
  ledger reads and writes and its character saves die at their lock timeout. Every later boot is a
  no-op. Dashboards should move to `accounted_rows`; `lifetime_inserted_rows` is a deprecated
  alias with the same value, and both can now fall because cascade deletes give capacity back, so
  any `increase()` or `resets()` alert on it must be re-expressed against the gauge
  (`DEPLOY.md`, "Hot paths and retention").
- Roll v0.42.0 out to every realm process in one pass, never staged across days. Farm plots, the
  Masterwrought daily gates, Perfecting markers, and every new content id ride the whole-blob
  character save, so a mixed fleet or a rollback past this release is destructive: a pre-farming
  binary erases planted crops and each character's Farming skill on its next autosave; an erased
  daily gate reopens Wyrmfall Core, daily craft, and Maker's Ember grants; a pre-Perfecting binary
  wipes a Perfected bonus through an ordinary replace-enchant (if a rollback must run, leave it
  running only with apply-enchant replace disabled); and old binaries drop new item and deed ids
  from discovery state. Treat a rollback across this release as a restore-from-backup event
  (`DEPLOY.md`, "Rollback caveats").
- Do not mix pre-Masterwrought or older standalone candidate server writers into the upgraded
  fleet; persistence is compatible from the professions release commit onward. The material-source
  writer capability (`woc.material_source_writer`, announced as a connection startup option) is
  enforced by triggers on every table that carries material composition, so an old binary's write
  is refused outright; rollout needs a coordinated stop and flush of old writers.
- The player-named legendary promotion prices names through the username ban screen. Seed
  `USERNAME_BANLIST_FILE` with the slur and hate-group residual the built-in word list does not
  carry before that feature is live; the file is capped at 64 KiB, an edit applies at the next
  name screen (a permissions-only repair also needs a `touch`), a missing or unreadable file warns
  once and keeps serving the last good list (fail-open, it never blocks a signup), and the file
  must live on local disk. A reported name is cleared with the SUPERADMIN, API-only endpoint
  `POST /admin/api/moderation/characters/:id/clear-item-name` (permission
  `moderation.clearItemName`): kick first, then clear, prefer `{"all": true}` with a reason, and
  remove the promotion's durable Discord activity card by hand. Only the name is stripped; the
  promotion, stats, signer, and bind stand. Under `API_DISPATCH=legacy` the endpoint is unavailable.
- During a realm-by-realm roll an old server still emits the retired "That item is already
  Perfected." line, which a new client renders untranslated; an older binary erases the
  `legendariesForged` deed counter until roll-forward; and a pre-promotion binary lets two promoted
  twins of one item be worn, which the first login after roll-forward benches to the bags.
  Fleet-wide in one pass avoids all three windows.
- The Rift Forge is open by default; set `RIFT_FORGE_ENABLED=0` (or false, off, no) to close it.
  The switch only works when the server sees the variable: `docker-compose.yml` forwards it through
  its per-key environment block, so a deploy template that renders its own compose must carry the
  same line. Existing Riftbound bands re-price onto the item-level ladder the first time they load.
- Per-surface action-bar layouts: deploy the server before the web and OTA bundles.
- The five shop mount skins render as unavailable until the companion economy service carries
  their `kind: skin` catalogue rows (woc-daily-rewards-service PR 33, five rows at 2000 Claudium).
  Activate the catalogue only after the compatible game server is live.
- Schema additions are additive and applied at boot: the `realm_builder_honours` table, the
  `accounts.discord_queue_pings` column (default false), and the GPU model, laptop, adapter, and
  backend columns on `client_perf_reports`. Guild bank log and action-bar documents stay readable

  fence refused because the character came back online; a refusal is silent and the remedy is to

  worker's active state and refusal cause across the client population.

The Crucible has a new soundtrack, with a dedicated track for each of its four floors.

- **Floor 3: A Fate Still Unwritten** carries the journey deeper into the Crucible.

Each floor's music continues through enemy pulls and boss combat. Moving between floors fades into the next track, and leaving the raid restores the normal world soundtrack. Music volume, mute and menu pause continue to work as usual.
