# World of ClaudeCraft - v0.19.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.19.0  
**Date:** 2026-07-03  
**Previous release:** v0.18.0  

v0.19.0 is a large gameplay and platform release with **59 commits** since v0.18.0. The headline is Talents 2.0, a casting overhaul that lands the deterministic primitives the choice-row talent redesign is built on (interrupt with a PvP consent gate, empower-next charges, and cast-while-moving) alongside a new ground-targeted casting mode with five aimed AoE spells. This cycle also ships wallet-gated Daily Rewards with a real-USD daily leaderboard, an Electron desktop app plus native store-update prompts, a client hot-path performance pass, whisper quality-of-life, and a from-scratch soundtrack recomposition.

## Highlights

- **Talents 2.0 casting foundation:** v0.19.0 lands the deterministic primitives for the choice-row talent redesign, interrupt (with a PvP consent gate and lockout diminishing returns), empower-next charges (an instant, a free, and a guaranteed-crit next cast), and cast-while-moving, all content-unused so the parity goldens stay byte-identical (#1305).
- **Ground-targeted casting:** five caster and ranged classes gain aimed AoE (mage Flamestrike, warlock Rain of Fire, hunter Volley, druid Hurricane, shaman Earthquake) on a new server-clamped targetMode 'position' primitive, with a desktop cursor reticle and a terrain-draped AoE impact ring (#1064).
- **Daily Rewards:** Players holding enough WOC in a verified wallet now earn points from a daily weighted spin (20 to 250) and server-credited quest, arena, and online-time tasks, then climb a per-realm daily leaderboard whose top 10 split a real-USD prize pool (20/15/12/10/9/8/7.5/7/6.5/5 percent), with the winners posted to Discord once per day (#1307).
- **Native store updates:** iOS and Android now prompt players to update through the App Store or Play Store, and the old Appflow over-the-air bundle swap is turned off (#1288, #1286).
- **Performance:** A client hot-path pass froze 1252 static terrain and prop matrices, fixed the scene root that defeated the freeze, warmed icons off the main thread, and trimmed 20 Hz decode and per-frame allocations, lifting an in-crowd measurement from 79.9 to 82.5 fps (#1254).
- **Soundtrack recomposed:** Every non-Eastbrook music cue was rewritten around per-place leitmotifs and multi-section forms, from Mirefen's waterlogged requiem to a rebuilt "Vanguard" battle theme, while the three Eastbrook Vale themes stay note-for-note identical and are now checksum-pinned (#1291).
- **Whispers rounded out:** a filter-only Whisper tab collects every whisper in one place and replies to the last whisperer with /r, a Whisper action lands in the portrait right-click menu, and a dev-only /dev bot spawns a whisperable auto-replying test dummy to exercise it all offline (#1313).

## Talents 2.0: Casting Overhaul and Ground Targeting

- **The casting foundation for the choice-row talent redesign.** v0.19.0 lands the deterministic casting primitives the Talents 2.0 rework is built on (design locked in docs/prd/talents-2.0.md: six class-wide choice rows at levels 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, and 20 that replace the old 234-node point trees). The primitives ship content-unused this cycle, so no row grants them yet and the 159 parity goldens are unmodified, but every future interrupt, mobility, and empowerment talent now has a real mechanic underneath it instead of a flat stat nudge (#1305).
- **Interrupt (#1305):** a new interrupt ability effect cancels a target's non-physical, non-fishing cast and applies the existing school lockout aura for the effect's lockout duration. The victim's cast resolves per-player when possible (rank and mods) with a global ABILITIES fallback, so a future mob caster is interruptible too, while a scripted pseudo-cast that is absent from the ability table resolves to nothing and stays immune by design.
- The interrupt primitive was hardened before any interrupt content ships: interrupting a non-consenting player outside a duel, arena, or fiesta (through the shared isHostileTo hostility model) is a full no-op with no cancel and no lockout; lockout durations route through diminishing returns under a new lockout DR category (full, half, quarter, immune on an 18 second reset window), and on DR immunity the cast still cancels but no lockout lands; and a new AbilityDef.uninterruptible flag protects an explicitly flagged cast (#1305).
- **Empower-next (#1305):** three one-charge self-auras in src/sim/combat/empower_next.ts. next_cast_instant makes the next cast-time spell instant (never a channel, never a physical cast); next_cast_free waives its cost, consumed exactly where the cost is billed (queue time for on-next-swing, cast start for channels and instants, completion for cast-time spells, and the conjure and revive early branches); and next_attack_crit forces the next damaging roll to crit while consuming the identical rng draw, so draw order and count are unchanged.
- **Cast-while-moving (#1305):** a new AbilityDef.castWhileMoving flag plus a per-ability talent transform (the Firestarter design) baked onto the resolved KnownAbility, so a flagged cast or channel survives the player's own movement. The move-input cast cancel skips a mobile cast, and fishing still cancels.
- **Conditional-effect primitives (#1305, also content-unused):** directDamage gains vsRootedMult (multiplies a hit against a rooted target, applied after the spell-power rider and before the crit multiplier), and a new critVsRooted global adds spell crit chance against rooted targets, read through the playerMods accessor so fiesta augment overlays compose; the crit roll stays a single rng draw with a different chance input. addEffects lets a talent append effect riders to an ability, shallow-copied before the scaling pass so they inherit the same modifiers as native effects and shared content arrays are never mutated.
- **Ground-targeted casting (#1064):** a new targetMode 'position' aims an ability at a world point instead of an entity. The client proposes the point and the server clamps it to the ability's range from the caster (authoritative) through a new castAt command; the cast's area effects (aoeDamage and groundAoE) center on that point, and with no point chosen the cast falls back to the caster's feet so existing callers are unaffected. The aim is stashed in Entity.castAim, clamped at cast start, and always cleared on resolve, cancel, or channel completion.
- Five thematic ground spells ship on the primitive, one per caster and ranged class, each fully translated across every locale with its own distinct procedural icon (src/ui/icons.ts): mage Flamestrike (learned at level 20), warlock Rain of Fire, hunter Volley, druid Hurricane, and shaman Earthquake (all learned at level 18) (#1064).
- Flamestrike is an instant aimed burst rather than a lingering zone (owner feedback: no dot on the floor): it detonates once at the range-clamped point for 34 to 44 Fire damage in a 7 yard radius (80 mana, 12 second cooldown, 30 yard range) and leaves no ground zone (#1064).
- Rain of Fire, Volley, and Hurricane are channeled ground AoEs that rain damage on the aimed area over the channel: Rain of Fire (fire, 4 ticks over 4 seconds, 14 to 18 per tick in a 7 yard radius), Volley (physical, scales off Ranged Attack Power, 6 ticks over 3 seconds, 12 to 16 per tick in an 8 yard radius, mitigated by armor), and Hurricane (nature, 6 ticks over 6 seconds, 12 to 16 per tick in an 8 yard radius). applyChannelTick pulses a position-targeted channel's AoE at castAim every tick, with physical channels mitigated by armor and spell-school channels not, mirroring the instant aoeDamage path (#1064).
- Earthquake stays an instant lingering nature zone (groundAoE, 13 to 17 Nature damage in an 8 yard radius over 6 seconds, pulsing every 1.5 seconds) (#1064).
- **Desktop ground-targeting reticle (#1064):** pressing a position-targeted ability opens aiming mode, a school-colored pulsing reticle ring that follows the cursor on the terrain via the click-to-move ground raycast, pre-clamped to the ability's range with the sim's own clamp math (dimmed when the raw cursor is out of range) and sized to the blast radius. Left-click or the same slot keybind commits castAbilityAt at the reticle, Escape or right-click cancels, and other actions cancel aiming first. The pure aim math lives in src/ui/ground_aim.ts with unit tests, behind a new Ground-Targeting Reticle option (Interface, on by default); mobile and reticle-off keep the quick-cast-at-target-or-feet behavior.
- The impact reads for the moment it matters and then gets out of the way: a new world-anchored spellfxAt event carries the blast radius, and the renderer flashes a school-colored, terrain-draped AoE ring under the burst (a pooled visual with a pure animation model in src/render/aoe_ring.ts, 0.7 second lifetime, mirroring click_marker.ts) with no lingering decal (#1064).
- **IWorld parity and determinism:** a new castAbilityAt(abilityId, aim) on IWorldCombat is implemented in both the offline Sim and the online ClientWorld (which sends the castAt command frame), so render and ui reach ground targeting only through IWorld and the world_api parity test is updated. The primitives draw no new rng and leave the 159 parity goldens byte-identical (#1305, #1064).
- Ground-spell impacts interest-scope correctly: the server's event anchor now anchors a world-coordinate spellfxAt event at its own x and z, so an impact reaches only players within EVENT_RADIUS instead of broadcasting realm-wide, exactly like its entity-anchored siblings (#1064).

## Daily Rewards

- **Wallet-gated daily rewards (#1307):** A new daily rewards system lets players who hold enough WOC in a verified wallet earn points from a daily spin and rotating tasks, then climb a daily leaderboard for a share of a real-USD prize pool. Eligibility is checked server-side as wallet WOC balance times the WOC to USD price against a configurable minimum (default 20 USD), and every reason (eligible, no_wallet, under_minimum, price_unavailable) is surfaced to the client so a locked wallet shows exactly why.
- **One spin per day, weighted outcomes:** The spin draws one of eight outcomes worth 20, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100, 150, or 250 points, at weights 25, 22, 18, 14, 9, 6, 4, and 2 (percent) respectively. A spin is one per account per reward day, enforced by the daily_reward_spins primary key and an ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING insert, so the endpoint returns 403 when the wallet is locked and 409 when the day's spin is already claimed.
- **Server-credited tasks:** Points from tasks are only ever credited server-side, never on a client's word. Completing a quest turn-in credits the default quest task (base 10 points), an arena match credits win or loss task points, and each credited minute of activity scales a task multiplier from 1 up to 3 (one step per 30 minutes online). All task credit is gated on wallet eligibility and made idempotent by a per-source key (for example task:<taskId>:quest:<questId>), and only players active within the configured window (default 120 seconds) accrue online minutes, recorded once per UTC minute on a 60-second server sweep.
- **Daily leaderboard and USD payout splits:** Points feed a per-realm daily leaderboard (tiebreak: earliest to reach the score). At day rollover the previous day is finalized and its top 10 are written to daily_reward_payouts with fixed prize splits of 20, 15, 12, 10, 9, 8, 7.5, 7, 6.5, and 5 percent of the pool (summing to 100 percent), against a configurable pool (default 150 USD). The game server records payout rows as pending only: it never transfers funds. An external private payout service reads pending rows via POST /internal/daily-rewards/pending-payouts and reports each result back with a transaction signature via /internal/daily-rewards/mark-payout, both guarded by a dedicated shared secret.
- **Discord winner announcements (#1307):** Once a day is finalized, the community bot posts a single gold embed titled "Top N Winners" to a dedicated achievements channel, listing each winner's rank, name, points, USD prize, and percent share alongside the realm and prize pool, then marks the day announced (daily_reward_days.discord_announced_at) so it is posted exactly once. If DISCORD_DAILY_REWARDS_CHANNEL_ID is unset the bot logs once and skips the feed. The winners feed is served over the existing secret-gated /internal/discord/* surface.
- **Runtime config lives off-server:** The reward minimum, prize pool, WOC and SOL prices, and the task list are owned by the private payout service and fetched from its GET /daily-config, cached with a configurable TTL (default 5 minutes). When the service origin is unset or unreachable the server falls back to safe built-in defaults (20 USD minimum, 150 USD pool, a single quest task) and logs the reason at most once a minute, so the feature degrades gracefully rather than failing.
- **Client-asserted task credit removed before ship:** An intermediate POST /api/daily-rewards/task route that credited a task's points on the client's assertion alone was removed as a security hardening, since points drive a real-USD leaderboard. The public API exposes only status (GET /api/daily-rewards), the spin (POST /api/daily-rewards/spin), and history (GET /api/daily-rewards/history); the daily_reward_task_completions table is retained (additive, with no writer) for task-completed display and a future server-verified completion path.
- **Configurable reward day start (#1310):** The reward day no longer flips at UTC midnight. A configurable day start (dayStartUtcMinutes, default 1260 minutes, that is 21:00 UTC) shifts the boundary, and a shared dailyRewardClock resolves the active reward day from that offset across status, spin, online, quest, and arena crediting and the finalize-previous-day rollover. New rewardDayForDate, addRewardDays, and nextUtcResetIso helpers (unit-tested) compute the day and the exact next reset instant.
- **Live reset countdown (#1310):** The rewards window now shows an "Ends in" countdown next to the reset time, repainted every 30 seconds and formatted as "<1m", "{m}m", or "{h}h {m}m" from the server's resetAt, so players can see how long is left in the current cycle.
- **Client surface and launcher (#1307):** IWorld gains dailyRewards, spinDailyReward, and dailyRewardHistory (src/world_api/daily_rewards.ts), implemented in ClientWorld over REST and stubbed as a locked, no-wallet status in the offline Sim so render and ui stay world-agnostic. A treasure-chest launcher button and the rewards window are mirrored into both the index and play entries; the button pulses "spin-ready" while a spin is unclaimed or the wallet is not yet eligible, and both are hidden entirely on the native mobile app.

## UI, Rendering, Input, and Performance

- **Home graphics selector (#1284):** The landing/start screen gains a Graphics dropdown, beside the language picker and the High Contrast toggle, so players pick a tier before entering the world instead of hunting through the Esc options. The choices are Auto, Low, Medium, High, Ultra, and Advanced, mapping to `graphicsPreset` 1 to 5 in `src/game/settings.ts` (Medium is the shipped default). Auto leaves `graphicsDefaultApplied` false so the renderer keeps probing a device-appropriate tier on each boot; picking a specific preset sets `graphicsDefaultApplied` true so first-run detection never overrides the choice. An out-of-range or unrecognized stored value normalizes back to Auto (`normalizedLandingGraphicsChoice`), and the control stays gameplay-neutral: presets only shed cosmetic richness, so choosing a lower tier before login never changes actionable information.
- **Painted resource and consumable item icons (#1202):** Resource and consumable items now render committed artwork instead of procedural glyphs. A new image-icon path (`ITEM_IMAGE_IDS` plus `itemImageUrl` in `src/ui/icons.ts`) mirrors the skill-icon system and is served for kind `item` across bags, tooltips, loot, vendor, and the /wiki guide; `iconDataUrl` prefers a weapon icon, then the item image, then the procedural recipe. 101 curated 128px webp icons under `public/ui/items/` cover food, drink, potion, elixir, junk, quest, and tool items (provenance and license in `public/ui/items/mapping.json`). Equipment stays on procedural icons, and any item id not in the set falls through to `ITEM_RECIPES`. Guarded by `tests/item_icons.test.ts`.
- **Hunter pet-bar icons no longer borrow class spell art (#1202):** The pet action buttons reused real class ability icon ids (`rejuvenation`, `defensive_stance`, `rapid_fire`, `growl`, `prowl`, `drain_life`), so a hunter's Aggressive stance rendered the same icon as their own Rapid Fire and Heal Pet showed the druid's green magic heal. A new `pet_action_icons.ts` module maps each command to a dedicated recipe (`pet_attack`, `pet_growl`, `pet_feed`, `pet_mend`, `pet_passive`, `pet_defensive`, `pet_aggressive`), and Heal Pet is renamed Feed Pet with a roasted-meat icon (hunters feed pets, they do not magic-heal them); the warlock still mends its demon. Guarded by `tests/pet_action_icons.test.ts`.
- **Gamepad presses count toward APM (#1311):** The perf overlay's actions-per-minute readout previously tracked only keyboard and mouse. The `GamepadManager` now fires an `onInputEdge` callback on every button rising edge (both in-world action dispatch and the virtual-cursor UI-navigation mode), recording one beat per press into the `InputActivityMeter` that reports every 10 seconds. The meter is constructed before the manager so the wiring exists at start. Guarded by `tests/gamepad.test.ts` (each rising edge is counted exactly once).
- **Static-matrix freeze and scene-root fix (#1254):** Three r165 recomposes and re-multiplies every node's matrices each frame by default, which on this scene is thousands of never-moving prop and terrain nodes paying real per-frame CPU. A new `src/render/static_matrix.ts` freezes a fully-built static subtree (one final `updateMatrixWorld`, then `matrixAutoUpdate` off), applied to the terrain group, the water meshes, and the props tree (1252 nodes frozen; the transform-animated campfire flames are re-enabled explicitly). The scene root is frozen to identity so frozen subtrees skip the world-matrix multiply too, not just the compose, and hidden (distance-culled, off-screen, or compile-gated) view groups set `matrixWorldAutoUpdate` false to skip their 30 to 60 node subtrees, re-opening the gate in the same sync before render so nothing renders stale. `pick()` skips hits on hidden views, and light-owning quest-object glow views are exempt from the gate. Measured in a 30-bot crowd: `multiplyMatrices` self-time 6.35% to 4.76%, combined matrix share 14.6% to 12.7%, fps 79.9 to 82.5; on a north-village walk `updateMatrixWorld` self-share fell from about 10% to 7%.
- **No more first-open icon freeze (#1254):** The first vendor, bags, or loot open used to pay a synchronous 60 to 300ms burst composing every visible item icon (canvas plus `toDataURL`). A new idle-time warmer (`src/ui/icon_prewarm.ts`) drains the whole item and ability catalog through `requestIdleCallback` slices right after boot, so the shared `urlCache` is hot before any window opens. The pump enforces a 6ms wall-clock budget checked before every icon (previously it checked between batches of 8, which could overrun by 60 to 100ms).
- **20 Hz aura decode churn cut (#1254):** `ClientWorld.applyWire` gains an aura decode fast path: when the wire aura ids line up index-for-index with the existing records (the common case, only remaining ticks counting down), it updates the records in place instead of allocating a fresh array plus an object per aura per entity at 20 Hz. Composition changes still rebuild, and preserved object identity matches the offline `Sim` contract. Pinned by snapshot tests covering identity reuse, field updates, rebuild on gain or shrink, same-length reorder, and optional-field clearing.
- **Per-frame work and GC churn trimmed across the client (#1254):** render collapses six per-entity aura `.some()` scans into one pass, reuses the entity's computed `d2` for the loot-sparkle cull, caches the selection-ring terrain drape by (x, z, scale) so a stationary target skips the per-vertex `groundHeight` resample, and adds a per-school projectile color cache that removes three `THREE.Color` allocations per bolt launch (keyed on `GFX.composer` so a tier flip rebuilds the HDR variants). Input gates the hover-cursor scene raycast behind a `HoverPickGate` (re-pick on pointer move, otherwise at most every 50ms), with the cursor kind still re-resolved per frame from live entity state. Net reuses the `applySnapshot` seen-set and updates the threat and cooldown Maps in place, removing per-entity Map allocations at 20 Hz. The HUD early-returns the compass when facing is unchanged, drops the combo-pip array spread for an indexed walk, and reuses the tooltip box size measured at show time so a mousemove no longer forces a reflow per event. The offline sim's UTC-day string is cached in `src/game/utc_day.ts` (recomputed at most once per second), and the sim skips the `pendingLootRolls` defensive copy on empty ticks.
- All #1254 work is behavior-preserving and visually identical: the changes shed only redundant CPU and GC, never actionable information, so the graphics-settings fairness invariant is untouched. Verified green against the parity gate (golden traces plus rng draw order), the architecture and HUD perf-budget guards, and the snapshots and bandwidth guards.

- Every non-Eastbrook music cue in `src/game/music.ts` was recomposed from scratch around per-place leitmotifs grown from each zone's look and lore, trading the old short loops for multi-section forms scheduled by the existing lookahead timer (#1291). The three Eastbrook Vale themes (`town_eastbrook`, `vale`, `vale_legacy`) are kept note-for-note identical and are now pinned by a sha256 checksum guard in `tests/music.test.ts` so their note data can never drift by accident, and the intro and dungeon-boss mp3 players are left untouched.

- The three dungeon crawls each received a dedicated theme: Hollow Crypt's "Sleep, Neighbors" (D minor over a phrygian creep, 100 bpm, a funeral bell over an unmoving pedal), Sunken Bastion's "The Drowning Dark" (E minor passacaglia, 116 bpm, a four-note lament ground bass under water textures piling on in four-bar tides), and Gravewyrm Sanctum's "It Breathes Below" (B phrygian, 126 bpm, heartbeat war-drums under an antiphonal cult chant).
- Thornpeak Heights' overworld now plays the dedicated `peaks` anthem instead of borrowing the legacy Vale wilderness cue: the `ZONE_MUSIC` `vale_legacy` override was removed (`ZONE_MUSIC` is now empty, so every zone plays its biome theme), the Thornpeak hub still plays the Highwatch town theme, and `vale_legacy` remains available as a layer but is no longer routed anywhere. The world-music selection test was updated to expect `peaks`.
- The battle cue was reworked into "Vanguard", an orchestral upgrade grown from the original combat cue's own DNA (the pounding D staccato eighth cell `[0,0,3,0,7,0,3,5]`, the timpani one, three, and-of-four pickup skeleton, and bare horn fifths) rather than a drum-kit song. Its first four bars are the original texture over a new bass shadow, then it terraces in octave agitato, war drums, and a rising-fourth war call, takes a half-step shock answered by low brass, marches bVI to bVII home, hits a three-bar tutti, and ends on a drop bar that strikes once, breathes for two beats, and relaunches the cell so chain pulls never hear a dead seam. `COMBAT_TRANSPOSE` was recalibrated to move the D-rooted cue onto each zone's tonal center. Three audition-only variants (`combat_classic`, `combat_wardrums`, `combat_steel`) were composed for the maintainer to pick from and then removed before release, so only the `combat` layer ships.
- BGM loudness was equalized with a measured per-theme trim table (`THEME_TRIM`). The Eastbrook town theme had been playing about 10 dB louder than the quietest cues (Fenbridge, vale), turning zone borders into volume cliffs. Each cue was rendered offline through the exact in-game chain and its gated windowed RMS computed (400 ms windows, windows more than 15 dB under the loudest gated out), then trimmed to the Eastbrook reference; after trims every cue measures within 0.6 dB of target. `MusicDirector.update` drives each layer's gain at `target * trim`, so crossfade behavior is unchanged and the composition data (including Eastbrook) is untouched: this is a mixing change only. New tests require an explicit trim for every registered theme and assert the layer gains are driven through the trim, not a bare 0 or 1.
- The marsh and Fenbridge voices were brought up to the Eastbrook timbre standard without touching their note data: both leads moved off the raw square-wave reed and near-sine pipe onto the Eastbrook flute at Eastbrook velocity, with a harp and hammered dulcimer for attack color, the piano voice was upgraded in place with a stretched inharmonic partial stack (7 partials) so exposed droplets shimmer, and a new detuned-saw oboe voice was added but kept unrouted. Five new synth voices land overall: piano, shaker, brassStab, cymSwell, and oboe.
- Two dev-only auditioning tools shipped with the score. `scripts/render_music.mjs` plus `scripts/music_render_entry.ts` render any theme to a WAV through an `OfflineAudioContext` in headless Chrome with the exact in-game mix chain (master, compressor, hall reverb, and per-theme trim). `music_editor.html` is an in-browser piano-roll editor served by the vite dev server at `/music_editor.html`: it loads the real `buildMusicThemes()` note data, plays it through the real synth and mix chain, and saves edits through a dev-only vite middleware (`POST /__music_editor/save`) into `src/game/music_overrides.generated.ts`, which `buildMusicThemes()` merges over the composed themes. Both the editor page and the save endpoint exist only under the dev server's `configureServer`, never in a production build.
- The `MusicDirector` `localStorage` read (the `ev_music_on` on/off flag) was hardened to fall back cleanly in sandboxed documents where the property access itself throws.

## Architecture and CI

- The IWorld seam is kept a genuine type-only sim import. `src/world_api/chat.ts` previously value-imported `OVERHEAD_EMOTE_IDS` from `sim/types` to back its `isOverheadEmoteId` guard, dragging the deterministic engine into the seam that is supposed to sit above `sim/` and pull it in for types only. It now derives its runtime id set (`OVERHEAD_EMOTE_ID_SET`, a `Set` built from the facet's own `OVERHEAD_EMOTES` list) so the sim import becomes `import type` with no behavior change (#1313, #1314).
- The same change fixes the seam-purity guard itself: `tests/architecture.test.ts` keyed its `SANCTIONED_VALUE_SIM_IMPORTS` allowlist by forward-slash path but looked it up with `path.relative()`'s OS-native separators, so it silently never matched on Windows. A new `posixRel()` normalizer restores the match, and because chat.ts no longer needs an exemption the allowlist is now empty (kept as the escape valve for a future legitimate case).
- Decoupling chat.ts's id set from `sim/types` is only safe while the two lists stay in lockstep, so an id added to `OVERHEAD_EMOTE_IDS` alone would silently fall out of `isOverheadEmoteId` and the emote wheel with no failure. An OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR commenting `/review` or `/suggest <focus>` on a pull request fires a new `ai-review-comment` job in `.github/workflows/pr-ai.yml`, gated on the commenter's `author_association` evaluated against the base repo (so a fork PR's own author cannot self-trigger it). # World of ClaudeCraft - v0.18.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.18.0  
**Date:** 2026-07-02  
**Previous release:** v0.17.0  

v0.18.0 is a large gameplay and platform release with **65 commits** since v0.17.0. The headline is a sweeping talent tooltip accuracy pass and buff rebalance that makes every talent across all 9 classes and 27 specs state its real numbers, alongside a new developer badges system that rewards contributors who land commits in the open-source repo. This cycle also delivers party and raid loot settings with master looter, a World Market expansion with realm-scoping, Discord guild auto-join, and a broad stability and infrastructure hardening pass.

## Highlights

- **Talents:** Every talent tooltip across all 9 classes and 27 specs now spells out the exact numbers its effect produces, buff-strengthening talents that previously did nothing now deliver their promised bonuses, and caster and raid buffs are rebalanced into percentage, party-wide values (#1039, #1038).
- **Buff tooltips online:** Buff and debuff hover tooltips now show real magnitudes online, so Aspect of the Hawk reads "Increases attack power by 20" instead of "by 0" and percent effects, DoTs, and absorbs all display their true values (#1220).
- **Developer badges:** Contributors who land commits in the open-source repo now earn cosmetic developer badges through a verified GitHub link, with five tiers, nameplate and inspect flair, and a new Developers leaderboard tab (#1086).
- **Loot and raid:** A new party and raid Loot Settings window surfaces the group's loot rules to everyone, and whole-group loot messaging broadcasts the full loot lifecycle with clickable item links (#1216).
- **World Market:** The World Market is now realm-scoped so realms stop clobbering each other's listings (#946), with a critical fix that preserves listings whose item id is no longer known (#947).
- **Discord:** Linking or logging in with Discord auto-joins the World of ClaudeCraft guild via guilds.join, so players land in the community server the moment they connect (#1192, #1204).
- **Items:** Gear now requires a minimum level to equip (#1020) and all potions share a global 2-minute cooldown shown on the action bar (#1024).
- **Server stability:** The server now terminates sessions on unbounded send backpressure (#950) and isolates each session in the broadcast, event, and tick hot loops (#949), so one stuck or faulty client can no longer OOM the process or starve every other player of snapshots.

## Combat and Talents

- Every talent tooltip across all 9 classes and 27 specs now spells out the real numbers its effect produces (#1039). A gate test (tests/talent_tooltip_accuracy.test.ts) enforces that a tooltip is never vague, never states a number the effect does not produce, and lists every effect magnitude. 85 vague tooltips now give per-rank numbers, and 5 incomplete tooltips (Guardian Favor, Arcane Focus, Improved Devotion Aura, Aspect of the Hawk, Fortitude) now describe every value.
- Buff-strengthening talents that previously did nothing now work: Improved Devotion Aura, Aspect of the Hawk, and Fortitude carried a damage modifier on pure buff abilities (which do no damage), so a new buffPct ability-mod now scales the buff itself, delivering the promised +20% armor, attack power, or stamina.
- Three effect and tooltip mismatches are reconciled: Lightning Reflexes now grants +10% Agility, Arcane Mind +8% Intellect, and Emberstorm is tuned from 12% to 10%. Barrage now cuts Concussive Shot's cooldown instead of buffing its negligible damage.
- Caster and raid buffs are rebalanced into percentage, party-wide values (#1038): Mark of the Wild (+5% all attributes), Arcane Intellect (+5% Intellect), Power Word: Fortitude (+5% Stamina), Blessing of Might (+10% attack power), Devotion Aura (+10% armor), and Battle Shout (+10% attack power). Battle Shout and Devotion Aura keep their exclusive-group mutual exclusivity.
- Spell Power now scales healing, not just damage: direct heals take the cast-time coefficient and HoTs take the per-tick coefficient, so healers can gear their output. A double-dip guard keeps a HoT that rides a direct heal (Regrowth) from scaling twice, and determinism is preserved (the rider consumes no rng draws).
- Armor debuffs are now non-stacking percentages combined by maximum: Sunder Armor at 2% per stack (10% at 5) and Faerie Fire at a flat 10%. Thorns scales with the druid's Spell Power, snapshot at cast. The shadow priest is retuned: SW:Pain, Mind Blast, and Mind Flay damage up, Mind Blast cooldown from 8s to 6s, and Mind Flay cost from 45 to 40.
- The character sheet gains a per-stat source breakdown, including the new Spell Power stat: hovering a stat shows a "Made up of" list of its upstream sources (Base, from an attribute, gear, buffs, and talents) so players can see exactly where each point comes from.
- Online buff and debuff hover tooltips now show real magnitudes (#1220). The server previously stripped an aura's value for everything except negative stat-saps, so positive buffs like Aspect of the Hawk read "Increases attack power by 0", percent effects showed a garbage "100%", and DoTs and absorbs read 0. The wire now carries value, value2, value3, tickInterval, and school for every value-bearing aura, and the fix also derives the unit-frame shield overlay online. It is backward compatible and changes only the server-encode and ClientWorld-decode seam.
- The classic threat pull-over boundary now respects a mob's actual size (#987). A challenger still pulls aggro above 110% of the tank's threat in melee or above 130% at range, but "in melee" was a flat 6 yards, which misclassified a player standing at a large boss's feet as ranged and wrongly required 130%. The boundary now uses the mob's size-scaled reach.
- The taunt and forced-target window now keeps counting down while a mob is stunned, so a stun no longer freezes the timer and unexpectedly extends how long a taunt holds.
- The Gravecaller Summoner (Zone 2 trash) loses its Wail of the Grave fear proc (#995). Mob-sourced crowd control bypasses diminishing returns, so the summoner stacked a full 4s silence and a full 4s fear on one victim with no safety valve. It keeps Silencing Shriek (4s silence) and Grave Blight (heal absorb), remaining a dangerous anti-caster without the double crowd control.

## Developer Badges

- Contributors who land commits in the open-source repo now earn cosmetic developer badges (#1086), mirroring the existing token-holder and Discord status-tier systems. The badges are purely cosmetic: the simulation never reads them.
- Players link a verified GitHub account through GitHub OAuth using a "Link GitHub" control beside the wallet-link row on character select, following the same flow as the existing Discord link.
- Landed-commit counts come from GitHub's public contributor stats for the repo, cached server-side with a 5-minute backoff after a failed fetch so a rate-limited API is not hammered.
- There are five rungs by landed commits: Tinkerer (1+), Artificer (10+), Runesmith (50+), Architect (150+), and Worldwright (500+), each with its own procedural "commit graph" SVG badge distinct from the holder coins and Discord numerals.
- Badges surface across the game: a glyph next to other players' nameplates (with a glowing name outline for Architect and above, composed on top of any Discord staff color), the inspect screen (badge, tier name, commit count, and @login), and the shareable player card PNG.
- The high-score window gains a third "Developers" tab that ranks contributors by landed commits alongside the existing Players and Guilds boards.
- Operators get telemetry: the contributor-stats cache and the link flow report fetch, hit, miss, failure, and link request and failure counts through the same admin provider-usage view as the token-balance and releases proxies.

## Loot and Raid

- **Loot Settings window (#1216):** A closable, reopenable window shows the group's loot rules. The leader edits the loot method (group loot or master looter) and the roll threshold, while members get a read-only view. It opens from the group-panel right-click menu and auto-opens when you become party leader, so a new group's loot rules are front and center. The window docks below the party frames and is draggable, and it never steals keyboard focus or closes your other windows.
- **Whole-group loot messaging (#1216):** The entire party or raid now sees setting changes (stating exactly what changed), a loot-settings summary sent to a joining member, the effective master looter changing on leave or promote, a re-announce on party to and from raid conversion, and the full loot lifecycle (rolling, won, assigned, passed) for premium roll-worthy items, each with a clickable item link.
- **Master looter curate window:** The master looter gets a 5-minute window to curate loot before it is distributed.
- **Promote to leader:** A new promote-to-leader social action lets you hand off group leadership, and master loot follows the handoff so the new leader controls distribution.
- **Raid lockout reset (#1031):** Raid lockouts are standardized to a single daily reset on us-east-1 time, so every raid shares one predictable reset schedule.

## Items

- **Minimum level to equip (#1020):** Gear now requires a minimum level to equip, derived from the item's power tier so higher-tier gear cannot be worn early.
- **Shared potion cooldown on the action bar (#1024):** All potions share one global 2-minute cooldown (the classic-era combat-potion value), now surfaced as a cooldown swipe and countdown on potion action-bar slots so players can see the shared timer at a glance. Quaffing one potion puts every potion slot on the same swipe.
- **Sell food and drink in stacks (#1022):** Food and drink can be sold in stacks of 5 at classic per-unit pricing.
- **Shift-click item links (#1027):** Shift-clicking an item inserts a clickable item link into chat, and this link infrastructure is reused by the new whole-group loot messaging.

## Server and Networking

- The game server now terminates any WebSocket session whose outbound buffer grows without bound, guarding against a single non-draining client (a frozen tab, a wedged proxy, or a deliberately non-reading peer) accumulating an unbounded send backlog and running the whole realm process out of memory (#950).
- Backpressure is enforced with a hard 8 MiB outbound-buffer limit in a pure, unit-tested helper (server/ws_backpressure.ts); a session over the limit is torn down through the existing close and leave path so the player is fully removed and can rejoin cleanly (#950).
- Each session is now isolated inside the broadcast, event-routing, and tick hot loops, so a throw while building or routing state for one player degrades to a single skipped session instead of starving every other player of snapshots and events that tick (#949).
- Per-session and per-tick bodies run through a host-agnostic guard (server/guarded_iter.ts) as defense in depth: a persistent fault is contained to one bad session, a transient fault still self-heals on the next tick, and the serialized snapshot and event payloads stay byte-identical (#949).

# World of ClaudeCraft - v0.16.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.16.0

**Previous release:** v0.15.0

v0.16.0 is a very large gameplay, systems, admin, performance, frontend, localization, native, and architecture release. It includes the `release/v0.16.0` line plus the post-v0.15.0 mainline refactor and modernization work that was merged before this release tag.

The headline player-facing changes are projectile damage on impact, a new Spell Power stat, item levels and item set bonuses, master loot, free-for-all corpse unlocks after a short owner lock, a second action bar, debuff separation, richer aura and item tooltips, cancelable player buffs, WebP class ability icons, major render freeze fixes, crowd LOD, a rebuilt Svelte 5 admin dashboard with moderation tooling, and native OTA/store polish.

The headline engineering changes are the SimContext extraction campaign, IWorld facet split, frontend HUD and CSS modernization, stronger accessibility infrastructure, graphics fairness gates, expanded localization to 21 locale files, full release i18n gates, private bot-detector Docker overlay support, and a much stronger QA/reviewer workflow.

## Highlights

- **Combat timing and spell resolution:** Projectile spells now deal damage on impact instead of on cast, spells are resisted instead of missed, Lightning Shield has a 3-charge cap and internal cooldown, hunter aspects are mutually exclusive, Wolf Form uses the rogue cadence, stun chains have diminishing returns, pets despawn on owner death, and ability/combat-potion cooldowns persist through logout.
- **Itemization and loot:** Added item levels with stat-budget normalization, item set bonuses, armor-type coverage requirements, armor type display in item tooltips, master loot, randomized tied rolls, probability validation, and a 1-minute owner lock before tapped corpses open to everyone.
- **HUD and player UX:** Added a second action bar, separated player debuffs from buffs, buff/debuff effect tooltips, right-click buff cancellation, targetable dead pets for menu recovery, improved aura classification, improved floating combat text plumbing, and a footer link to the public whitepaper.
- **Performance:** Fixed open-world travel freezes with constant point-light counts and render prewarming, added a generic async compile gate for new content, added crowd-adaptive character LOD for populated zones, reused render animation buffers, and throttled arena snapshot readouts.
- **Admin and moderation:** Rebuilt the admin dashboard around Svelte 5 and added moderation detail pages, account/IP association tooling, blocked IP flows, chat filter management, moderation history, provider usage, bug report views, and broad test coverage.
- **Native and release packaging:** Added OTA update support, store polish, iOS/Android metadata updates, app icons, Capacitor live-updates dependency, and mobile release documentation.
- **Architecture:** Shrunk the Sim coordinator behind a SimContext seam, split `IWorld` into facet interfaces, extracted large HUD/render view cores and painters, moved CSS into structured `src/styles` layers, and added standing architecture, parity, UI purity, perf, accessibility, and localization guards.

- Projectile damage now resolves when the projectile impacts the target rather than when the cast starts. This fixes the classic-feel timing problem where a spell could land before the visible projectile arrived.
- Added projectile travel modeling and tests for impact timing, no-escape behavior, and chart/screenshot generation.
- Spells now use resist outcomes rather than miss outcomes. This makes spell combat line up with classic-era rules and separates spell resolution from physical hit tables.
- Added Spell Power as an Intellect-derived caster damage stat, with spell-scaling support, tooltip/readout plumbing, tests, and screenshot tooling.
- Added debuff attack power handling into player attack power for PvP so attack power reductions apply correctly against players.
- Added stun diminishing returns to stop chain-stun lockouts in PvP and other repeated-control scenarios.
- Lightning Shield is capped at 3 charges with a 5-second internal cooldown, including charge display/supporting tests and screenshots.
- Direct damage is now the only damage that can move a mob's leash anchor, preventing Lightning Shield from enabling unlimited kiting.
- Hunter aspects are mutually exclusive, with tests covering aspect replacement and exclusion behavior.
- Wolf Form now swings at the rogue cadence instead of using the carried staff cadence.
- Rogue Stealth and Vanish now apply the intended 50% movement speed behavior, and stealth movement penalties were aligned in content.

- Hunter and warlock pets despawn when their owner dies.

# World of ClaudeCraft - v0.11.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.11.0
**Date:** 2026-06-21
**Previous release:** v0.10.0

v0.11.0 is a security, localization, wallet, performance, and polish release with
**80 commits** since the public v0.10.0 tag. It removes the vulnerable third-party
wallet connector stack, adds a smaller injected Solana wallet-linking path,
introduces `$WOC` holder flair and shareable player cards, completes a major
hardcoded-string localization sweep, improves graphics budgets and telemetry,
and lands several game-feel fixes across movement, audio, market browsing, and
combat.

## Highlights

- **Wallet security cleanup**: the Reown/AppKit wallet SDK stack was removed and
  replaced with a narrow injected Solana wallet flow for challenge signing.
- **Zero moderate-or-higher npm audit findings**: the latest release branch audit
  reports `found 0 vulnerabilities`.
- **$WOC holder flair and player cards**: linked wallets can show exact `$WOC`
  balance, holder-tier badges, shareable player cards, and referral-friendly
  card URLs.
- **Full hardcoded-string localization sweep**: UI, sim, server, admin, and
  generated locale outputs were hardened so player-facing text continues to pass
  release-tier localization gates.
- **In-game language switching**: players can switch language from the Options
  menu without leaving the game.
- **Graphics budgets and telemetry**: adaptive render budgets, low graphics
  profile tuning, telemetry export, and performance reporting tools were added.
- **Market browsing improvements**: search, filters, filtered counts, styled
  filter menus, and pagination make listings beyond the wire cap reachable.
- **Game-feel fixes**: Druid Travel Form and Dash now provide real movement
  speed, hill descent stays grounded, final DoT ticks apply, target portraits are
  sharper, and footstep audio no longer produces a metallic jingle.

  `@solana/web3.js`, and the associated browser polyfill path from the wallet
  client dependency surface.
- Wallet linking now uses injected Solana browser wallets directly. The flow is
  intentionally narrow: detect a provider, connect, sign the server challenge,
  and send the signature back for account linking.
- The wallet UI is enabled by default and can be disabled with
  `VITE_WALLET_DISABLED=1`.
- `$WOC` balance reads now go through the server proxy so RPC keys do not ship to
  the browser.
- Wallet UX was refined around Wallet Standard behavior, late provider injection,
  signature encoding, disconnect/account-change events, and wallet-help text
  alignment.
- Third-party license notices were added for the removed wallet-connect stack so

  player-card persistence, and card sharing helpers.

  images continue to use the dev origin.

  exact balance support, and quality-pass test coverage.

## World of Claudecraft v0.3.0

This release is a major online-play update focused on social systems, moderation,
combat behavior, performance, and the first-pass release polish for the public game.

### Highlights

- Added friends, guilds, ignores, and realm-aware social systems.
- Added player reporting and admin moderation tools.
- Added right-click reporting from chat player names.
- Added a classic MMO-style threat system for tanking and deaggro.
- Polished the title screen, login flow, character creation, and character preview.
- Added hashed media caching for faster repeat loads.
- Added in-game community links.
- Included recent trade, chat, options, movement, and performance fixes.

### Social

- Added a Friends panel with add/remove, presence, zone/status display, and whisper
shortcuts.
- Added ignore/block support, with blocked players filtered server-side.
- Added guild creation, invites, ranks, guild chat, officer chat, promote/demote,
kick, leader transfer, leave, and disband flows.
- Added WoW-style realm list support, with realm-scoped characters, guilds, friends,
and character names.

### Moderation

- Players can now report other players in game.
- Players can right-click chat names to report, ignore, whisper, friend, invite to
party, or invite to guild.
- Chat right-click menus intentionally exclude Trade and Challenge to Duel, since
those are live nearby-player actions.
- Reports are resolved server-side by live player id or realm-scoped character name.
- Admin moderation tools now support report review, ignore report, suspend, ban, and
force rename.
- Reports include recent chat context where available.

### Combat And Gameplay

- Added a classic threat model so mobs can change targets based on damage, healing,
taunts, pets, and tank actions.
- Added deaggro/leash behavior so mobs do not stay locked forever.
- Added tank-oriented behavior for warriors, druids, paladins, and hunter pets.
- Preserved rogue stealth behavior, including stealth visibility/detection handling.
- Improved immediate bag refresh after trade.
- Fixed trade item duplication issues.
- Added invite lockout protections so party, duel, and trade invites do not
overwrite each other unexpectedly.

### Chat

- Added separate chat and combat log windows.
- Improved scrollback behavior.
- Added chat rate limiting and ignore actions.
- Persisted accepted chat logs to Postgres with retention.
- Logged accepted chat channels only.

### UI And Options

- Polished the title screen and online/offline entry flow.
- Added 3D character preview.
- Improved class selection hover/focus behavior.
- Added a game options menu for key bindings, graphics, and audio.
- Improved character select layout.
- Added in-game community invite links.

### Performance And Infrastructure

- Added hashed media caching for safer long-lived asset caching.
- Added retained hashed media output under `/media`.
- Improved movement jitter behavior.
- Added identity deltas, retained entity lists, and distance-tiered update rates to
reduce town/crowd lag.
- Added spatial hash grid support for entity radius queries.

### Admin Notes

- New admin moderation views are available through the admin dashboard.
- Production deploys should include generated hashed media assets.
- The release was integrated through `release/v0.3` and promoted through `dev-0.3`
to `main`.

### Known Notes

- Electron desktop builds are not part of this release.
- Mobile support is not a focus for this release.

Apache Storm 2.8.7 has been released. This release includes critical security fixes, library updates, and documentation improvements. **The community strongly encourages all users of previous versions to upgrade to this release.**

### ⚠️ Security Fixes

*   **CVE-2026-40557: JVM-wide TLS Security Downgrade in Prometheus Reporter**
    *   **Versions Affected:** 2.6.3 to 2.8.6.
    *   **Technical Description:** Enabling the `skip_tls_validation` configuration in the Prometheus Reporter caused an improper certificate validation that replaced the default SSL context. This resulted in a JVM-wide TLS security downgrade, affecting all components within the same process.
    *   **Fix:** The reporter now uses a scoped SSL context for validation bypass, ensuring the default JVM SSL context remains secure.
*   **CVE-2026-41081: Improper Handling of TLS Client Authentication Failures**
    *   **Versions Affected:** All versions before 2.8.7.
    *   **Technical Description:** When TLS client authentication was enabled, failed authentication attempts were incorrectly assigned a fallback "ANONYMOUS" principal. This allowed unauthorized users to potentially bypass authorization checks that relied on the presence of a principal.
    *   **Fix:** Connections are now strictly rejected if TLS client authentication fails or is missing when required.

This release includes two security fixes, enhancements, bug fixes, and a large number of dependency upgrades. Users of previous versions are strongly encouraged to upgrade.

⚠️ Security Fixes

CVE-2026-35337 — Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Storm

Versions affected: < 2.8.6

When processing topology credentials submitted via the Nimbus Thrift API, Storm deserializes the base64-encoded TGT blob using ObjectInputStream.readObject() without any class filtering or validation. An authenticated user with topology submission rights could supply a crafted serialized object in the "TGT" credential field, leading to remote code execution in both the Nimbus and Worker JVMs.

Fix: Upgrade to 2.8.6. If you cannot upgrade immediately, monkey-patch an ObjectInputFilter allow-list to ClientAuthUtils.deserializeKerberosTicket() restricting deserialized classes to javax.security.auth.kerberos.KerberosTicket and its known dependencies. See the full mitigation instructions in the release notes.

Credit: Discovered by K.

CVE-2026-35565 — Stored XSS via Unsanitized Topology Metadata in Storm UI

Versions affected: < 2.8.6

The Storm UI visualization component interpolates topology metadata (component IDs, stream names, grouping values) directly into HTML via innerHTML in parseNode() and parseEdge() without sanitization. An authenticated user with topology submission rights could craft a topology with malicious HTML/JavaScript in component identifiers, resulting in stored cross-site scripting. In multi-tenant deployments this enables privilege escalation through script execution in an admin's browser session.

Fix: Upgrade to 2.8.6. If you cannot upgrade immediately, patch storm-webapp/src/main/webapp/js/visualization.js to escape output in parseNode() and parseEdge(). See the full mitigation instructions in the release notes.

Credit: Discovered while investigating another report by K.

### Security

- `Object::unwrap` and `Object::remove_wrapped` (and the deprecated `Env::unwrap` / `Env::drop_wrapped`) read a `TypeId` out of a payload that is not a `TaggedObject`, giving a heap out-of-bounds read and a JavaScript-forgeable out-of-bounds write; payload provenance is now validated before dereferencing. See [GHSA-rhpj-pggq-896v](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/security/advisories/GHSA-rhpj-pggq-896v), fixed in [#3506](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3506).
- The serde deserializer reached `unreachable!()` on ordinary JavaScript values and aborted the process instead of returning an error. See [GHSA-f334-75xc-qxv3](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/security/advisories/GHSA-f334-75xc-qxv3), fixed in [#3507](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3507).
- `ArrayBuffer::from_external`, `TypedArraySlice::from_external` and `Uint8ClampedSlice::from_external` (plus the compat-mode `Env::create_arraybuffer_with_borrowed_data`) built their slice from freed memory on runtimes without external buffers. See [GHSA-32mm-r9wp-hrvc](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/security/advisories/GHSA-32mm-r9wp-hrvc), fixed in [#3503](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3503).

### Fixes

- **WASI threads builds on current toolchains** ([#3492](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3492))
  `wasm32-wasip1-threads` was failing in two ways: wasi-sdk 34 changed the futex ABI, and Rust nightly started linking `crt1-reactor.o` itself (duplicate `_initialize`). The CLI now picks the matching emnapi archive; the build crate stops double-linking `_initialize`.

- **WASI on Android / Termux** ([#3485](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3485))
  Generated Node loaders preopened `/`, which Termux cannot open (`UVWASI_EACCES`). Android now preopens the current working directory. Other platforms are unchanged.

- **Generated files share one format** ([#3501](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3501))
  JSON / TOML / YAML, `.d.ts`, and JS / WASI loaders now use one house style (indent, trailing newline, quotes). Regenerating bindings may produce noisy diffs with no behavior change.
